items.title: Baltic states try secret dip into EU defense purse – media
items.summary: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania have secretly asked the EU for more money for drone defense, the Finnish newspaper Iltalehti has reported Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Baltic states try secret dip into EU defense purse – media
The Baltic states have secretly asked the European Commission for hundreds of millions of euros to boost their defense against drones, citing an alleged Russian threat, the Finnish newspaper Iltalehti has reported.
Moscow has repeatedly rejected claims that it has aggressive designs against Europe, saying that they are only made by Western politicians to scare the population at home and justify growing military spending. It maintains that a conflict is only possible if NATO members attack Russia.
Iltalehti said on Tuesday, citing foreign policy and security sources, that the defense ministers of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania had sent a letter to EU chief Ursula von der Leyen the previous day, asking Brussels to urgently provide them with €500 billion (around $570 million). There has been no public announcement about the request being made, it added.
The minister claimed that the funds are needed due to the possibility of Russia trying to test NATO’s resolve by carrying out drone strikes against the bloc’s eastern flank, the report read.
Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius expect a positive response from von der Leyen in a matter of weeks, with the money arriving by the end of the year, according to the sources.
Last week, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that Russia could fire drones or missiles into NATO countries backing Ukraine in “the next few months.” Despite Tusk providing no proof to his claim, French President Emmanuel Macron described it as “sound and well-documented.”
On Tuesday, Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius told the BBC that his country feels “constantly threatened” by Russia because of drones entering its airspace.
Since spring, there have been a number of incidents of Ukrainian UAVs crossing into Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia or crashing in their territory as Kiev has intensified its long-range attacks on energy infrastructure in Leningrad Region in northwestern Russia.
The Baltic states claimed that the incursions happened because of the UAVs being diverted off course by Russian electronic warfare equipment. Moscow has warned Tallinn, Riga and Vilnius that it could act in accordance with its right to self-defense if it turns out that the three countries are knowingly providing their airspace to the Ukrainian military.
Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics claimed in an interview with the Kiev Independent the same day that his country is facing an “alarming” period due to possible Russian interference in the wake of an election on October 3.
On Wednesday, high-ranking Estonian Foreign Ministry official Jonatan Vseviov said that warnings of an alleged Russian attack on the Baltic states were “blown out of proportion.” According to Vseviov, Moscow “ultimately seeks… to change the entire European security architecture,” but it’s currently fully focused on the Ukraine conflict.
Russian President Vladimir Putin said last week that “some European leaders are openly declaring that they are preparing for war with Russia” in an attempt to “cover up mistakes in their economic and social policies.”
“Instead of stopping and listening to their citizens, who have made it clear during the elections that they don’t want any war with Russia, these leaders continue to escalate the situation,” Putin stressed.

items.title: Drug cartels recruiting drone operators with Ukraine conflict experience – WaPo
items.summary: Mexican drug cartels are increasingly relying on drone operators with Ukraine conflict experience, the Washington Post has reported Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
Drug cartels recruiting drone operators with Ukraine conflict experience – WaPo
Mexican drug cartels are increasingly relying on drone operators who have returned home after taking part in the Ukraine conflict, the Washington Post has reported, citing US and Mexican officials.
Russia has warned repeatedly that the Ukraine conflict is fueling global instability as it leads to proliferation of weapons supplied by the West to Vladimir Zelensky’s government on the black market and fosters reckless behavior by Kiev in pursuit of its war aims.
The WaPo reported on Tuesday that Mexican cartels are closely studying ways to evade anti-drone jamming systems and are purchasing advanced UAV models that can carry more cargo and explosives.
In order to operate their expanding drone fleet, drug traffickers have intensified efforts to hire individuals with Ukraine conflict battlefield experience, mainly Colombian nationals, using both financial incentives and coercion, a US official told the paper.
A Mexican official also said that Colombian UAV experts are being brought to Mexico by criminal organizations to train large groups of local “droneros,” or drone pilots.
Colombians make up around half of the estimated 16,500 foreign mercenaries currently fighting for Ukraine, a security source told TASS in June. They are being lured into the ranks of Kiev’s forces with false promises of high pay, he said. The Latin Americans end up being treated with disdain by their Ukrainian commanders, fed poorly, and deployed on the most dangerous missions, the source added.
The cartels are also sending their own “affiliates” to join the Ukrainian military and gain battlefield experience of flying drones, a US official said.
Drug traffickers “are going to be way better off, way better trained, with way better equipment,” the official warned.
Washington expects cartels to implement drone skills and tactics borrowed from the Ukraine conflict within the next several months, according to the sources.
An internal government assessment suggests that the development will “significantly complicate” the campaign by the administration of US President Donald Trump to curb the flow of illegal drugs into the country, an American official noted.
The US State Department said in a statement to the WaPo that it’s working with American law enforcement agencies and the Ukrainian authorities “to adopt measures to mitigate the risk of battlefield skills transfer,” and that Washington itself relies on experience from the Ukraine conflict to “counter the cartel drone threat.”
Last year, the Milenio newspaper cited Mexican intelligence as saying that members of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) had received training in drone and urban warfare tactics in Ukraine.
CNN reported earlier this month that around 15 Ukrainian drone operators have been embedded with the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) in Mali to train the members of the militant group and assist them in fighting government forces and Russian troops stationed in the West African country.

items.title: UK makes military pledge to Saudi Arabia
items.summary: Britain will deploy an RAF tanker to Saudi Arabia as fighting with Yemen’s Houthis intensifies, the UK government has said Read Full Article at RT.com
items.body_text:
UK makes military pledge to Saudi Arabia
The UK has pledged military assistance to Saudi Arabia as tensions with Yemen’s Houthis intensify, citing growing risks to regional trade and energy supplies.
Hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, who control much of northern Yemen, have intensified in recent weeks after several years of relative calm. The Houthis have launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi territory, while Riyadh-backed government forces have battled the group inside Yemen.
Britain will deploy an RAF Voyager air-to-air refueling aircraft to the region following a request from Riyadh. The aircraft will provide refueling support for Saudi “defensive activity” in Yemen, the Ministry of Defense said on Tuesday.
Riyadh has reportedly sought military assistance from several countries as its stocks of missile interceptors come under pressure. US President Donald Trump reportedly considered strikes on the Houthis over the weekend after Riyadh sought direct American military action, but ultimately held off. Washington has instead provided Riyadh with intelligence and targeting data.
The Houthis have made major gains along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, seizing the port of Mokha and strategic islands around Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow strait linking the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden. The group, which is also known as Ansar Allah, has targeted Saudi-linked shipping and demanded that Riyadh lift its blockade of Yemen before negotiations.
Bab el-Mandeb has taken on greater importance as traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted by the US-Iran war. US government data show oil flows through Hormuz fell from 21.6 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 4.9 million bpd in the second quarter of this year, while volumes through Bab el-Mandeb rose from 5.4 million to 8.1 million bpd over the same period.
The disruption around Hormuz has already rattled global energy markets, while the renewed fighting in Yemen has raised concerns over another major shipping route. Brent crude surged to nearly $110 a barrel earlier this month after drone attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West pipeline, a key route for bypassing Hormuz.
The UK is already facing renewed price pressures from the energy shock. Inflation rose to 3.1% in August, driven in part by higher fuel costs, with the Bank of England warning that it is likely to rise further over the coming quarters.
London already has personnel and air-defense equipment stationed in the kingdom and has previously taken part in strikes against the Houthis. RAF Typhoons supported by Voyager tankers joined US operations in Yemen in 2024 and 2025, after the Houthis began attacking Israel and vessels in the Red Sea during the Gaza war.
London has also provided military assistance to Saudi Arabia since a Saudi-led coalition first intervened in Yemen in 2015, after the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and forced the internationally recognized government into exile.
Large-scale Saudi-Houthi fighting subsided following a UN-brokered truce in 2022, although no permanent settlement was reached. Washington and the group separately agreed to stop targeting each other under an Oman-mediated deal in May 2025.

items.title: Russian Regions Slowly Reimpose Fuel Purchase Limits Amid Ongoing Refinery Attacks
items.summary: The new restrictions come after Ukraine struck major oil refineries in Moscow, Samara and Ufa over the past three days.
items.body_text:
A growing number of Russian regions have recently seen the reintroduction of fuel rationing measures to combat shortages of gasoline and diesel caused by Ukrainian drone strikes against major oil refineries throughout the country.
In the Kaluga region southwest of Moscow, Governor Vladislav Shapsha announced the return of an odd-even system based on vehicle license plate numbers and a ban on sales into portable canisters starting Wednesday.
“The lines [at gas stations] are back. This causes reasonable frustration,” Shapsha wrote on Telegram.
In Siberia’s Zabaikalsky region, authorities announced a cap of 15 liters (4 gallons) per vehicle on AI-92 and AI-95 gasoline grades across 48 gas stations. Fuel reserves in the region stood at 17,000 metric tons, which are expected to run out in 20 days.
Zabaikalsky’s regional government stressed that 106 out of its 249 functioning gas stations were selling fuel without any restrictions.
Both announcements follow Ukrainian drone attacks on three key Russian oil refineries in Moscow, Samara and Ufa over the last three days. The Ukrainian military claimed this week that it has knocked out more than 45% of Russia’s refining capacity.
Last week, authorities in the Leningrad region surrounding St. Petersburg capped gasoline sales at 30 liters (8 gallons) per vehicle until at least Oct. 1. They described the region as the epicenter of a second wave of Russia’s summer fuel crisis after Ukrainian attacks on the Kirishinefteorgsintez (KINEF) refinery knocked it offline in August.
Nearly one in five independent and small gas stations had suspended work because they have been unable to buy wholesale fuel on the St. Petersburg exchange, Leningrad region Governor Alexander Drozdenko said.
Drozdenko said oil companies expect fuel supplies to stabilize in October.
The average price of gasoline in Russia has climbed 21% since the start of the year, with a single-week increase pushing the national average to 78.51 rubles per liter ($3.39 per gallon) as of Sept. 14.
Russia has banned gasoline exports through Jan. 31, 2027, along with diesel until the end of October, to stabilize the domestic fuel market.

items.title: EU Removes Billionaires Usmanov and Fridman From Sanctions List
items.summary: The EU also rolled over the remaining 3,000 individuals and entities on its Russia sanctions list for another three years, diplomats said.
items.body_text:
EU diplomats agreed Tuesday to drop billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from the bloc's Russian sanctions list and to roll over the remaining 3,000 individuals and entities for another three years.
Earlier this month, France shocked other EU members when it pushed for Russian-Uzbek metals tycoon Usmanov to be removed from EU sanctions, citing national security concerns. Luxembourg then demanded the same treatment for Fridman, who has launched a $16 billion claim against the country.
As a compromise, EU envoys agreed to remove the two billionaires in exchange for a three-year renewal of measures against the other sanctioned individuals and entities instead of the usual six months.
Latvia was the last holdout in an unusually fraught process. The deadline to renew the sanctions was at midnight on Sept. 22 after an extension from the original expiry on September 15.
Sanctions require unanimity among EU countries to be approved. Latvia ultimately abstained, diplomats said, which allowed the deal to pass. The decision was formally approved via a process known as a written procedure later on Tuesday.
"The decision to delist Usmanov and Fridman is shameful and unjustifiable. Moscow is celebrating," Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said in a post on X, urging EU countries to impose their own national restrictions on the two men.
Latvia's Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said Riga would look to impose its own sanctions. He added that France had agreed to start talks with Latvia about joining a French nuclear deterrence initiative.
The episode has roiled European leaders who had hoped to present a more united front against Russia since a recent change of government in Hungary. Former Hungarian leader Viktor Orban was a frequent obstacle to sanctions and support for Ukraine.
It took high-level meetings in Europe and on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this week to iron out the agreement, diplomats said.
The EU imposed sanctions on both men in 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which include transaction and travel bans in the EU and a freeze on assets held in the bloc.
Latvia had previously taken legal action to maintain EU sanctions on Fridman and his Russian-Latvian business partner Petr Aven. For Riga, Fridman's connection to Aven is a sore point, diplomats said.
Aven was stripped of the country's highest civilian honor in 2022 for not condemning Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
France came under pressure from Azerbaijan, where at least two French nationals are detained, three European diplomats told Reuters last week.
They added that Paris had indicated in private that Baku was using Usmanov to "blackmail" it over the case of two French citizens held in Azerbaijan, an assertion rejected by Baku.
Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev has previously lobbied for Usmanov's delisting, though it remains unclear why he did so.

items.title: Rapper GeeGun reportedly opened fire on staff at his Moscow home several months ago. He denies it.
items.summary: The Telegram channels Mash and Shot, as well as Ksenia Sobchak, said rapper GeeGun (real name Denis Ustimenko) opened fire on staff at his home in the Moscow region in the early hours of July 4.
items.body_text:
Rapper GeeGun reportedly opened fire on staff at his Moscow home several months ago. He denies it.
The Telegram channels Mash and Shot, as well as Ksenia Sobchak, said rapper GeeGun (real name Denis Ustimenko) opened fire on staff at his home in the Moscow region in the early hours of July 4.
According to Shot, the rapper fired from “an air gun resembling a “Saiga-9” [a rifled carbine].”
Mash writes that the rapper “called the staff into the living room and took the law into his own hands.” He accused one guard of pedophilia and shot him, wounding him in the arm and leg. He accused the rest of the staff of “betrayal, leaking information, nationalism, and other things.” According to the Telegram channel, GeeGun “held the household staff and guards hostage for about 10 hours” in front of his children.
Ksenia Sobchak writes that the children of GeeGun and his ex-wife, Oksana Samoilova, “were saying goodbye to her [their mother] and thought their father would shoot them along with the staff” (Samoilova was abroad at the time; her eldest daughter called her). Police, the gated community’s security, and GeeGun’s friends were called to the property. About 10 hours later, after the rapper “was subdued,” he was sent to rehab in Israel for several months.
Caution: the quote below contains profanity.
GeeGun himself confirmed to the Telegram channel Super that he is in rehab and called reports of the shooting “bullshit and a provocation.” “Let them write whatever they want. I was filming a snippet, and the haters twisted everything,” the rapper said.

items.title: Russia’s financial watchdog proposes freezing bank accounts over partial matches with ‘terrorists and extremists’ list
items.summary: Russia’s Federal Financial Monitoring Service, known as Rosfinmonitoring, is proposing to expand the grounds for freezing bank accounts. Under the proposed amendments, banks would be able to halt transactions when a client’s data only partially matches the data of a person whose funds are subject to a freeze.
items.body_text:
Russia’s financial watchdog proposes freezing bank accounts over partial matches with ‘terrorists and extremists’ list
Russia’s Federal Financial Monitoring Service, known as Rosfinmonitoring, is proposing to expand the grounds for freezing bank accounts. Under the proposed amendments, banks would be able to halt transactions when a client’s data only partially matches the data of a person whose funds are subject to a freeze.
The amendments to Russia’s law on combating the legalization of criminally obtained income were published on the government’s portal for draft regulations. The outlet Frank Media drew attention to the document.
Banks currently must freeze the accounts of people on Rosfinmonitoring’s list of terrorists and extremists within 24 hours. The list includes more than 15,000 people, including Telegram founder Pavel Durov, writer Boris Akunin, and political scientist Ekaterina Schulmann.
If the amendments pass, banks would halt transactions for five business days when a partial match occurs. The freeze would be lifted unless a separate decision extends it during that period. Rosfinmonitoring itself would set the exact criteria for what counts as a match.
As of February 1, 2026, more than 800 people on Rosfinmonitoring’s list had multiple recorded variants of their name, surname, or other identifying information, according to the document. The amendments are meant to close the loophole that allows people to evade the restrictions.

items.title: 'Arrest poll panel chief': Mamata demands Bengal repoll amid EC 'SIR split' row
items.body_text:
She said that INDIA bloc will meet soon amid concerns over the "issue"
NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday demanded fresh Assembly elections in West Bengal using the pre-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list while announcing pan-India protests against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, after a report claimed two Election Commissioners had raised objections to aspects of the voter-roll revision exercise.Reacting to a media report, Mamata demanded Kumar's arrest and accused the Election Commission of working in favour of the BJP."Re-election must be held in West Bengal with the old voter list," Banerjee said during a Facebook Live, adding that there would be "pan-India protests till Gyanesh Kumar remains CEC". "It has now been proven that the BJP and the EC looted the West Bengal assembly polls," she alleged.
Mamata also called for Kumar to be arrested, saying, "He must be immediately arrested and put behind bars. The chair of the CEC is not for a person like him.""This is such a scandalous story. We had never seen this in our lives. This Election Commissioner must be arrested. He has no moral authority to continue," she said, referring to the report.The TMC leader said INDIA bloc partners had discussed the issue and would meet soon.Meanwhile, in another TMC pushback, national general secretary and MP Abhishek Banerjee separately accused the election commission of deliberately deleting 30 lakh voter names from West Bengal electoral rolls to benefit the BJP.
He alleged that similar manipulation had taken place in Haryana and Bihar and demanded the immediate arrest of Kumar."The allegations we raised earlier have today been echoed by the other Election Commissioners as well. Just as the names of 30 lakh people were deleted from the voter list to benefit one political party, the same was done in Haryana and Bihar," Abhishek alleged.Abhishek also questioned the process through which Kumar was appointed, citing a split Supreme Court verdict on the Election Commission selection panel and the dismissal of an impeachment motion moved by Opposition parties.The Election Commission, however, said that "operational queries or inputs" had been raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on matters including the SIR exercise, but maintained that these related to the draft stage and were part of "standard administrative practice aimed at safeguarding voter rights". The poll panel also said decisions relating to the SIR were taken unanimously with the approval of all three Election Commissioners.
The row erupted when a media report claimed that Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR, including some that they allegedly said were taken without their knowledge.

items.title: 'Deliberations sign of pure democracy': BJP reacts to EC 'SIR split' row, targets Cong
items.summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra defended the Election Commission's internal discussions as a sign of democracy. He accused opposition parties, particularly Congress, of undermining constitutional institutions due to electoral defeats. Patra highlighted that criticism of the Election Commission indicates a broader campaign against democratic bodies. He emphasized that the opposition's attacks are inappropriate and calls into question their respect for established institutions.
items.body_text:
He said opposition parties had questioned the functioning of the three election commissioners both when they appeared to agree and now when correspondence between them has emerged.
NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday defended the election commission over the row surrounding an alleged split among the poll panel's commissioners, with party MP Sambit Patra saying that internal deliberations between the three election commissioners were a sign of a healthy democracy. He also accused the Congress of attacking constitutional institutions after failing to win elections.Addressing a press conference, Patra referred to the EC's press note and said correspondence among the three election commissioners had taken place on 14 occasions."I am not here to hold a press conference on behalf of the Election Commission. I have brought the press note issued by the EC, and I have read it. I hope you have also read it," he said.Patra said the correspondence showed that the commissioners had formally exchanged views and consulted one another.He added, "But now there has been correspondence among the three commissioners on 14 occasions. This is official deliberation among the three election commissioners. What do we gather from this? The BJP did not go and plant a story in the media saying that there had been official deliberations among the three commissioners.
Such deliberations are actually a sign of a healthy democracy..."
Patra targets opposition
Patra also hit out at opposition parties over their criticism of the EC, accusing them of attacking constitutional institutions.He said opposition parties had questioned the functioning of the three election commissioners both when they appeared to agree and now when correspondence between them has emerged."If the three election commissioners who conduct elections in the country do not communicate with each other, do not exchange views or consult one another, and simply keep agreeing with each other, then the Opposition parties say, 'This is a dictatorship.'"
"They say, 'This government appointed all three of them, and they simply keep saying yes to everything. They are all supporters of Modi.'"Patra said the opposition had also used the term "Godi media" for sections of the media and was now making similar allegations against the poll panel."You say the same thing about the media, calling it 'Godi media', and now you say these three commissioners are also 'Godi' people."
Congress accused of attacking institutions
Patra linked the latest controversy to what he described as a broader Congress campaign against constitutional institutions."You know how, since 2014, when the Modi government came to power, opposition parties have been falling one after another. They did not fall on a battlefield, but in the democratic arena, as their existence came under threat because they were not chosen by the people," he said.
He claimed the Congress had subsequently turned its focus to institutions after finding itself unable to win elections.He added, "After that, particularly the Congress party realised that it could not win elections, and so the biggest weapon in its hands was to 'kill the institutions of the country'. It began attacking our constitutional institutions and trying to defame them."Patra said the criticism of the EC was part of the same campaign, "In the same context and as part of the same campaign, several parties have held press conferences today regarding the Election Commission."

Each leader arrives with their own strategic advantages in the realms of trade and technology, potentially shaping the discussions ahead. The intricate matters concerning Taiwan and rare earth supply chains will add layers of complexity to the talks.
items.body_text:
The handshake will last seconds. The bargaining could shape the next phase of the world's most consequential rivalry.
When Donald Trump and Xi Jinping sit down in Washington on September 24, neither man arrives empty-handed. Trump can threaten tariffs, restrict China's access to American technology and wield the world's dominant financial system. Xi can retaliate through China's vast manufacturing base, its grip on rare earths and its economic relationships with countries Washington wants to pressure.
Also read: Five reasons India should watch Trump-Xi handshake
There is a useful historical precedent for the idea that US-China summits are less about friendship than mutual necessity. When Richard Nixon travelled to Beijing in 1972, Washington and Beijing were still formally estranged after more than two decades of hostility. Yet both had strategic reasons to talk. The United States wanted to reshape the Cold War balance against the Soviet Union; China wanted to counter Moscow and break out of its diplomatic isolation. The resulting Shanghai CommuniquÃ© did not erase their disagreements, particularly over Taiwan. It created a framework for managing them. Seven years later, Washington and Beijing established formal diplomatic relations.
More than half a century later, the question is not who is stronger. It is who has the better cards on the issues that matter most.
Here are five cards Trump and Xi bring to the table:
A fragile truce, not a friendship
Trump's second term began with tariffs on Chinese goods justified partly by concerns over fentanyl trafficking. China retaliated, and the confrontation escalated through 2025 as both sides imposed tariffs and export restrictions. By the autumn, Trump was threatening tariffs as high as 100% on Chinese imports, while Beijing was tightening controls on critical minerals and rare earths.
The May agreement gave Trump several concrete commitments to point to, but the key question is how much of Beijing's pledge has actually translated into deliveries.
The confrontation eventually produced a truce. At their meeting in Busan in October 2025, Trump and Xi agreed to reduce some tariffs and export restrictions, while China agreed to suspend expanded rare-earth controls and take measures against the export of fentanyl precursor chemicals. The arrangement eased immediate pressure without resolving the underlying disputes.
The May 2026 meeting in Beijing produced another round of commitments. The two sides agreed to establish Boards of Trade and Investment, while China committed to buying American agricultural products and 200 Boeing aircraft. But progress since then has been mixed. Chinese purchases of US farm goods have fallen short of the levels promised, the Boeing commitment has yet to materialise fully, and the investment board has moved slowly.
That is the backdrop to Washington: Not a new partnership, but a relationship that has stabilised just enough to keep functioning.
Trade: Trump's tariffs vs Xi's resilience
Trump's most obvious card remains the US market.
America is still one of the world's largest consumer economies, and Chinese exporters have a great deal to lose if access to it becomes significantly more expensive. Washington can therefore threaten to raise tariffs again if Beijing fails to deliver on existing commitments.
The November deadline gives Trump another lever. The current trade truce is due to expire then, creating a natural point at which tariffs and other restrictions could be revisited.
US imports from China have fallen sharply since 2024, but the trade deficit remains substantial.
Xi's counter-card is resilience.
China has taken a substantial hit to direct trade with the US, but it has not responded by capitulating. Instead, Chinese exporters have increasingly looked to other markets, while Beijing has retained control over several products and supply chains that American industry still needs.

items.title: Yemen's Houthis to target U.S. interests if it supports Saudi-led strikes: Houthi military adviser
items.summary: While the Yemen civil war predates the U.S.-Iran war by years, renewed fighting in Yemen pits allies of Washington and Tehran against each other while the two foes are stalemated in the Gulf
items.body_text:
A Houthi military adviser told AFP that the group would attack U.S. interests in the West Asia if Washington intervenes in Yemen's conflict in support of Saudi Arabia or tries to unblock the Bab al-Mandab strait.
The Iran-backed Houthis seized control of the narrow shipping lane, gateway to the Red Sea, this month, while Saudi Arabia has reportedly requested American and international military assistance against them.
"If America dares to intervene militarily with its fleets or tries to take control of Bab al-Mandab, it is a red line for them and anyone else... we will fight over it," military adviser Abed Mohammed al-Thawr told AFP in an exclusive interview on Tuesday (September 22, 2026).
The Houthi blockade has shaken Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, which was already hit by Tehran's strangehold on the strategic Strait of Hormuz as part of its war with the United States.
The pro-Iran Houthis dislodged Saudi-backed government forces from Yemen's Red Sea coast in fighting that left hundreds dead. Houthi drones and missiles have also targeted Saudi sites, including the capital Riyadh for the first time in years.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman requested help from U.S. President Donald Trump in fighting the Houthis, according to U.S. reports. Yemen's government also made the request, a well-placed source told AFP.
The Houthis say Saudi Arabia has conducted hundreds of strikes in Yemen since fighting resumed in July, effectively ending a four-year truce.
Iron fist
"If America gambles on supporting Saudi Arabia with airstrikes or air support... We will consider any American interests around us to be targets and we will not exclude anything," military adviser Thawr told AFP, adding that they will "close Bab al-Mandab completely to American ships".
While the Yemen civil war predates the U.S.-Iran war by years, renewed fighting in Yemen pits allies of Washington and Tehran against each other while the two foes are stalemated in the Gulf.
Thawr denied receiving directives from Iran, but said they are "one alliance and one body".
"Iran is a friendly, allied, and brotherly country to us, but it does not direct us. We are independent in our decisions and in our sovereignty," he said.
The United Nations on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) said the number of people displaced could swell from over 1,30,000 today to more than 2,30,000 in the coming months.
"As long as Saudi Arabia insists on and continues killing our country and striking our people, we will strike with an iron fist," Thawr said.
"We possess sufficient capability to discipline Saudi Arabia, punish it, and force it out of the game in the fields of oil and the economy."

items.title: Afghan female cyclist wins silver at Asian Games after disguising herself as a man to train
items.summary: The easy part for Fariba Hashimi was winning a silver medal in the women’s cycling road race at the Asian Games
items.body_text:
The easy part for Fariba Hashimi was winning a silver medal in the women's cycling road race at the Asian Games.
The nearly impossible part for the female cyclist from Afghanistan was trying to train in her country. To do that, she dressed as a man in a place where women have few rights. “All the time when I was going to training,” she said, “I was dressing as a guy.” She said she also hid her face when she could in order to not be recognised.
Aslo Read: UN experts condemn crackdown on women by Afghan morality police
“Because sometimes when they recognised me, they were trying to throw stones or hitting me," she said.
Hashimi won silver Tuesday in a time of 2 hours, 50 minutes, 5 seconds, which marked another leg in a journey that began in 2021 when she left Afghanistan.
“In 2021, when the Taliban moved into my country, I escaped my country because I wanted to follow my dream,” she said. “I want to show the Afghan women in the world that.... we can have an opportunity.”
Hashimi talked about having many dreams for women in Afghanistan, dreams for herself and dreams that may take time to be realised.
“I’m really, really happy and I’m full of emotion. I don’t know how I can explain it for you,” she said.
“I hope one day I come back in my country and ride the streets of Kabul — and riding with the women side by side to share the same passion," she explained.
“And I hope in the future to change some things,” she added. “I think we are really tired of the situation in our country, and I hope the Taliban is watching. I know how much one woman can be powerful and that's why the Taliban is scared of women.”
Published - September 23, 2026 05:42 pm IST

items.title: Easter Sunday blasts case: Sri Lankan court sentences each convict to 220 years in prison; all 15 to appeal against verdict
items.summary: A three-judge bench found that 14 of the accused were guilty on all charges, while a 15th defendant was found guilty of only some of the charges. Nine others were acquitted
items.body_text:
Fifteen people, sentenced to over 200 years each in prison by a Sri Lankan court for their involvement in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings, will appeal their record jail sentences, a defence lawyer said on Wednesday (September 23, 2026). This comes a day after the court found 15 of the 24 accused guilty of involvement in the attacks which killed 279 people.
Nine suicide bombers belonging to the local Islamist extremist group National Thawheed Jamaat, linked to ISIS, carried out a series of devastating blasts that tore through three Catholic churches and as many luxury hotels on April 21, 2019, killing nearly 270 people, including 11 Indians, and injuring over 500.
The fifteen accused have been sentenced to 220 years of rigorous imprisonment each by the Colombo Permanent High Court Trial-at-Bar. The court also ordered the confiscation of their movable and immovable property by the State.
The three-judge High Court Trial-at-Bar comprising Judges Navaratne Marasinghe, Ramanathan Kannan and Sujeewa Nissanka on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) found that 14 of the accused were guilty on all charges, while a 15th defendant was found guilty of only some of the charges. Nine others were acquitted.
Also read: The inside story of the 9 suicide bombers behind Sri Lanka’s savage Easter attacks
Defence Counsel Kneel Maddumage, who represented seven accused, said they would appeal the convictions as well as the record terms in the Supreme Court after receiving the relevant documents.
"Some of the defendants are not represented by counsel, but I requested on behalf of all the convicts that they be provided with copies of the proceedings to file their appeals," Mr. Maddumage said.
Initially, 25 people were charged over their role in the bombings. Following the death of one of the accused, 24 were indicted in October 2021.
A total of 23,270 charges were brought against them, while 2,309 witnesses testified for the prosecution.
Catholic Church spokesman Father Jude Krishantha welcomed the verdict, saying it has brought a sense of justice to the victims. "We feel satisfied because the relatives of those who died were expecting justice," he said.
In July, former Defence Ministry bureaucrat Hemasiri Fernando and former police chief Pujith Jayasundara were sentenced to death for failing to act on prior intelligence that could have prevented the attacks.
Published - September 23, 2026 05:24 pm IST

संजय भाटिया राजस्थान, बिप्लब देव एमपी के भाजपा प्रभारी:36 राज्यों-UTs की लिस्ट जारी; स्मृति ईरानी, राम माधव समेत 5 चेहरों को दो-दो राज्यों की जिम्मेदारी
- कॉपी लिंक
भाजपा ने बुधवार को 36 राज्यों-केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में पार्टी के नए प्रभारियों और 24 राज्यों में सह-प्रभारियों का ऐलान किया। संजय भाटिया को राजस्थान और बिप्लब कुमार देव को मध्य प्रदेश का प्रभारी बनाया गया है। राजस्थान में पहले डॉ. राधा मोहन दास अग्रवाल प्रभारी थे। वहीं, मध्य प्रदेश की जिम्मेदारी डॉ. महेंद्र सिंह के पास थी।
नई लिस्ट के मुताबिक, स्मृति ईरानी को छत्तीसगढ़ और हरियाणा का प्रभारी बनाया गया है। राम माधव को तमिलनाडु और उत्तराखंड की जिम्मेदारी दी गई है। तीन अन्य नेताओं को भी दो-दो राज्यों का प्रभारी बनाया गया है। बिहार में हरीश द्विवेदी को प्रभारी बनाया गया है। यूपी में 4 सह-प्रभारी नियुक्त हुए हैं।
UP-पंजाब-गुजरात के प्रभारी नहीं बदले, 18 अगस्त को हुई थी नियुक्ति
भाजपा ने उत्तर प्रदेश, पंजाब और गुजरात के प्रभारी नहीं बदले हैं। विनोद तावड़े उत्तर प्रदेश, सतीश पूनिया पंजाब और तरुण चुघ गुजरात के प्रभारी बने रहेंगे। इन तीनों नेताओं की नियुक्ति 18 अगस्त को ही की गई थी। उस समय पार्टी ने कहा था कि बाकी राज्यों के प्रभारी और सह-प्रभारी बाद में नियुक्त किए जाएंगे।
अब नई लिस्ट में इन तीनों राज्यों और उनके प्रभारियों के नाम फिर से शामिल किए गए हैं। ये तीनों राज्य 2027 में विधानसभा चुनाव वाले 7 राज्यों में शामिल हैं। इनके अलावा उत्तराखंड, गोवा, मणिपुर और हिमाचल प्रदेश में अगले साल चुनाव होंगे।
12 राज्यों-केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में कोई सह-प्रभारी नहीं
12 राज्यों-केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में भाजपा ने कोई सह-प्रभारी नियुक्त नहीं किया है। इसमें अंडमान-निकोबार, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, चंडीगढ़, दादरा नगर हवेली एवं दमन और दीव, लद्दाख और लक्षद्वीप शामिल है। मणिपुर, मिजोरम, नगालैंड, पुडुचेरी, सिक्किम और त्रिपुरा में भी सिर्फ प्रभारी नियुक्त किए गए हैं, कोई सह-प्रभारी नहीं है।
एंटनी प्रभारी और सह-प्रभारी दोनों बने, यूपी में 4 सह-प्रभारी बने; 4 खास फैक्ट्स
- 5 राज्यों में दो-दो सह-प्रभारी: असम, बिहार, दिल्ली, राजस्थान और तमिलनाडु में दो-दो सह-प्रभारी नियुक्त किए गए हैं।
- महाराष्ट्र में 3 सह-प्रभारी: बैजयंत जय पांडा प्रभारी हैं। वहीं, अमित मालवीय, सदानंद शेट तनवाडे और कमलजीत सहरावत सह-प्रभारी बनाए गए हैं।
- अनिल एंटनी को दो राज्यों में दोहरी जिम्मेदारी: अनिल एंटनी नगालैंड के प्रभारी बनाए गए हैं। वे गोवा के सह-प्रभारी भी होंगे।
- UP में 1 प्रभारी के साथ 4 सह-प्रभारी: विनोद तावड़े को प्रभारी बनाया गया है, जबकि उनके साथ चार सह-प्रभारी नियुक्त किए गए हैं।

- Hindi News
- National
- Rahul Gandhi Targets Election Commission Over SIR Process Controversy
रिपोर्ट-SIR पर 2 चुनाव आयुक्तों ने 14 बार आपत्ति जताई:आयोग बोला- यह सामान्य प्रक्रिया; राहुल ने कहा- वोट चोरी में शामिल, तो नहीं बख्शेंगे
- कॉपी लिंक
चुनाव आयोग ने बुधवार को स्पेशल इंटेंसिव रिवीजन (SIR) को लेकर चुनाव आयुक्तों में मतभेद से जुड़ी रिपोर्ट को खारिज कर दिया। चुनाव आयोग ने कहा कि पिछले एक साल में लिए गए सभी फैसले सर्वसम्मति से हुए हैं।
आयोग ने कहा कि किसी भी संस्थान में विचार-विमर्श के दौरान अलग-अलग राय और टिप्पणियां आना सामान्य प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा है। इसका उद्देश्य पारदर्शिता बनाए रखना और कानूनी नियमों का पालन सुनिश्चित करना है।
इस मामले में राहुल गांधी ने वीडियो जारी कर वोट चोरी को संविधान के खिलाफ बताया है। उन्होंने कहा कि समय आने पर किसी को छोड़ा नहीं जाएगा।
दोनों चुनाव आयुक्तों ने आपत्तियां ज्ञानेश कुमार को भी भेजीं
चुनाव आयुक्तों में मतभेद का विवाद द इंडियन एक्सप्रेस की रिपोर्ट के बाद शुरू हुआ। यह रिपोर्ट 23 सितंबर को पब्लिश की गई। इसके मुताबिक, चुनाव आयोग के दो चुनाव आयुक्त सुखबीर सिंह संधू और विवेक जोशी ने कहा कि कई फैसले उनकी जानकारी या मंजूरी के बिना लिए गए।
आयोग के फैसलों पर 28 अक्टूबर 2025 से 14 अगस्त 2026 के बीच 14 बार लिखित आपत्ति जताई गईं। इनमें 16 अप्रैल को चार आपत्तियां दर्ज की गईं। इन आपत्तियों की प्रतियां मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ज्ञानेश कुमार को भी भेजी गईं। कुछ आपत्तियां उन उप चुनाव आयुक्तों को भी भेजी गईं, जो संबंधित काम की निगरानी कर रहे थे।
यह विवाद बिहार से जून 2025 में शुरू हुए स्पेशल इंटेंसिव रिवीजन (SIR) के बीच सामने आया है। SIR के तहत 30 राज्यों और केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों की ड्राफ्ट मतदाता सूचियों से 13 करोड़ से ज्यादा नाम हटाए गए हैं।
अखिलेश ने कहा- सुप्रीम कोर्ट नोटिस ले, आप बोली- सुधार जरूरी
- राहुल गांधी- मैं इलेक्शन कमीशन और इलेक्शन ऑफिसर्स को साफ कह रहा हूं कि आप जो कर रहे हो गलत कर रहे हो। ये राजद्रोह है, देश के खिलाफ है। टाइम आएगा। हम आपको पकड़ेंगे। बचने वाले नहीं हो।
- सपा प्रमुख अखिलेश यादव- सभी चुनाव आयुक्त अपना सही काम नहीं कर पा रहे हैं। एक स्वतंत्र निकाय के सदस्यों को अगर न्यायपूर्ण कार्य करने की स्वतंत्रता नहीं है या उनकी कोई सुनवाई नहीं है तो ये लोकतंत्र के लिए बेहद घातक और खतरनाक हालात हैं। कुछ लोगों द्वारा सत्ता की कठपुतली बनकर लोकतंत्र को धोखा देना घोर सांविधानिक अपराध है। ये लोकतंत्र को मिटाने के किसी षड्यंत्र से कम नहीं है। सुप्रीम कोर्ट मामले की खुद जांच करे।
- AAP के राष्ट्रीय संयोजक अरविंद केजरीवाल- वोटर लिस्ट में नाम जोड़ने और हटाने का अधिकार सिर्फ ERO को है, फिर दिल्ली में बैठे लोग पूरे देश की वोटर लिस्ट कैसे बदल रहे हैं?
- ममता TMC की राज्यसभा सदस्य सागरिका घोष- SIR की खामियों और अव्यवस्था’ की जिम्मेदारी मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त की है। किसके निर्देश पर नागरिकों को कथित तौर पर मताधिकार से वंचित किया जा रहा है।
- UBT शिवसेना चीफ उद्धव ठाकरे- महाराष्ट्र, पश्चिम बंगाल और तमिलनाडु में बैलट पेपर का उपयोग करके फिर से चुनाव होने चाहिए।
- आम आदमी पार्टी के नेता सौरभ भारद्वाज- सभी विपक्षी दलों को पहले चुनाव आयोग से जुड़े इस मुद्दे को उठाना चाहिए और आयोग को व्यवस्थित करने पर ध्यान देना चाहिए।
ज्ञानेश कुमार को हटाने का पुराना मामला
अप्रैल 2026 में कांग्रेस नेता जयराम रमेश ने दावा किया था कि विपक्ष के 73 राज्यसभा सांसदों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) ज्ञानेश कुमार को हटाने के लिए नोटिस दिया है। इसमें ‘साबित कदाचार’ का आरोप लगाया गया था।
कांग्रेस महासचिव केसी वेणुगोपाल ने भी उनके खिलाफ कार्रवाई की मांग की थी। उन्होंने SIR के दौरान असली वोटर्स के प्रभावित होने का आरोप लगाते हुए सुप्रीम कोर्ट की निगरानी में जांच की मांग की थी।
इससे पहले लोकसभा में भी हटाने का प्रस्ताव दिया गया था, लेकिन लोकसभा अध्यक्ष ओम बिरला और राज्यसभा सभापति सीपी राधाकृष्णन ने इसे खारिज कर दिया था।
10 राज्यों और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में पूरा हुआ SIR
SIR के पहले और दूसरे फेज में 10 राज्य और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेश कवर हो चुके हैं। SIR के बाद बिहार, पश्चिम बंगाल, पुडुचेरी और असम विधानसभा चुनाव में भाजपा जीती है। केरल में कांग्रेस गठबंधन और तमिलनाडु में TVK ने जीत हासिल की है। असम में स्पेशल रिवीजन (SR) हुआ। यहां भी भाजपा सरकार की वापसी हुई।
तीसरा फेज: दिल्ली, महाराष्ट्र समेत 16 राज्यों में SIR
चुनाव आयोग ने 14 मई को हरियाणा, झारखंड, उत्तराखंड, दिल्ली और महाराष्ट्र समेत 16 राज्यों और 3 केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में स्पेशल इंटेसिव रिव

मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) और दो चुनाव आयुक्तों की नियुक्ति से जुड़े 2023 के कानून पर सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने बुधवार को बंटा हुआ फैसला दिया। जस्टिस दीपांकर दत्ता और जस्टिस सतीश चंद्र शर्मा की बेंच को यह तय करना था कि केस बड़ी (पांच जजों की) बेंच को भेजा जाए या नहीं।
5 दिन तक मामले की सुनवाई के बाद जस्टिस दीपांकर दत्ता ने केस 5 जजों की बड़ी संविधान बेंच को भेजने के प्रस्ताव को खारिज कर दिया। वहीं जस्टिस शर्मा ने इस प्रस्ताव को मंजूरी दे दी। हालांकि दोनों जजों ने मामला CJI सूर्यकांत के पास भेजने पर सहमति जताई है।
अब CJI तय करेंगे कि इस मामले की सुनवाई के लिए बड़ी बेंच बनाई जाए या नहीं। बेंच ने बड़े संवैधानिक मामलों की सुनवाई के लिए स्थायी 5 जजों की संविधान बेंच बनाने की संभावना तलाशने का भी अनुरोध किया है।
क्या है चुनाव आयुक्तों की नियुक्ति से जुड़ा मामला
मध्य प्रदेश महिला कांग्रेस कमेटी की महासचिव डॉ. जया ठाकुर, एसोसिएशन फॉर डेमोक्रेटिक रिफॉर्म्स (ADR) समेत कई याचिकाकर्ताओं ने चीफ इलेक्शन कमिश्नर एंड अदर इलेक्शन कमिश्नर्स (अपॉइंटमेंट, कंडीशंस ऑफ सर्विस एंड टर्म ऑफ ऑफिस) एक्ट, 2023 की संवैधानिक वैधता को चुनौती दी है।
विवाद इस बात को लेकर है कि 2023 के कानून में CEC और EC की नियुक्ति करने वाली चयन समिति में CJI को शामिल नहीं किया गया है। कानून के मुताबिक समिति में प्रधानमंत्री, प्रधानमंत्री की ओर से नामित एक केंद्रीय मंत्री और लोकसभा में नेता प्रतिपक्ष शामिल होते हैं। नेता प्रतिपक्ष नहीं होने पर लोकसभा में सबसे बड़े विपक्षी दल के नेता को मेंबर बनाया जाता है।
मार्च 2023 में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने CJI वाली कमेटी की व्यवस्था दी थी
2 मार्च 2023 को सुप्रीम कोर्ट की 5 जजों की संविधान बेंच ने कहा था कि CEC और EC की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति करेंगे। इसके लिए प्रधानमंत्री, लोकसभा में विपक्ष के नेता और CJI की कमेटी की सलाह ली जाएगी। कोर्ट ने यह व्यवस्था तब तक लागू रहने की बात कही थी, जब तक संसद इस बारे में कानून नहीं बना देती।
इसके बाद दिसंबर 2023 में संसद ने नया कानून बनाया। 29 दिसंबर 2023 को राष्ट्रपति ने इसे मंजूरी दी। नए कानून में CJI की जगह प्रधानमंत्री की ओर से नामित केंद्रीय मंत्री को चयन समिति में शामिल किया गया।
जस्टिस दत्ता बोले- आयोग स्वतंत्र हो, लोगों को स्वतंत्र दिखे भी
जस्टिस दत्ता ने कहा कि निष्पक्ष चुनाव के लिए चुनाव आयोग का स्वतंत्र होना जरूरी है। सिर्फ आयोग का स्वतंत्र होना ही काफी नहीं है, बल्कि लोगों को वह स्वतंत्र नजर भी आना चाहिए। उन्होंने कहा कि 2023 का कानून CJI को चयन समिति से बाहर रखने की सीधी चुनौती से शायद बच जाए, लेकिन उसे आयोग की स्वतंत्रता को लेकर लोगों की धारणा की कसौटी पर भी खरा उतरना होगा।
जस्टिस दत्ता ने यह भी कहा कि याचिकाकर्ताओं की यह दलील पहली नजर में कुछ आधार रखती है कि 2023 का कानून नियुक्ति की प्रक्रिया में कार्यपालिका को ज्यादा ताकत देता है। इससे संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 और संविधान की मूल संरचना में चुनाव आयोग की स्वतंत्रता से जुड़े सवाल उठते हैं। हालांकि उन्होंने इन सवालों पर कोई अंतिम निष्कर्ष नहीं दिया।
जस्टिस दत्ता ने कहा- पीएम के नामित व्यक्ति से अलग रुख की उम्मीद मुश्किल
जस्टिस दत्ता ने चयन समिति में प्रधानमंत्री की ओर से नामित केंद्रीय मंत्री की भूमिका पर भी सवाल उठाए। उन्होंने कहा कि जिस मंत्री को प्रधानमंत्री ने समिति में शामिल किया है, उससे अपने ही नामितकर्ता के खिलाफ जाने की उम्मीद करना मुश्किल है।
उन्होंने मंत्रिपरिषद की सामूहिक जिम्मेदारी का भी जिक्र किया। उनके मुताबिक ऐसी स्थिति में केंद्रीय मंत्री चयन समिति में उस स्वतंत्र संतुलन की भूमिका नहीं निभा पाएगा, जो किसी निष्पक्ष सदस्य से उम्मीद की जाती है। जस्टिस दत्ता ने इसी संदर्भ में कहा कि विपक्ष के नेता की मौजूदगी से भी चयन प्रक्रिया में जरूरी स्वतंत्र संतुलन हासिल नहीं हो सकता।
जस्टिस शर्मा बोले- 2023 में स्पष्ट व्यवस्था नहीं थी, अब संसद कानून बना चुकी

items.title: Who filed appeals on ECI's behalf? Row after report flags Bengal SIR anomaly
items.summary: Who filed appeals on ECIs behalf Row after report flags Bengal SIR anomaly
items.body_text:
Who filed appeals on ECI's behalf? Row after report flags Bengal SIR anomaly
An investigative report has flagged that two Election Commissioners objected to the ECI filing appeals against 16 lakh voters in Bengal whose names judicial officers had decided to retain in the electoral roll. It has sparked a massive controversy in Bengal.
Nowhere was the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls more contentious than in West Bengal. Now, an Indian Express investigation has found that questions over the handling of the SIR process came from within the poll panel itself. According to the report, one of the Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, objected to the filing of appeals against voters whose names judicial officers had decided to retain.
This was among the various aspects of the SIR exercise that were objected to by the two Election Commissioners over the past 10 months. The poll body, however, said the "differing views" were a normal part of deliberations.
The report has sparked a political furore in Bengal, where the BJP secured a historic win in the April elections, ending the 15-year reign of the Trinamool Congress. While Mamata Banerjee sought repolls in Bengal, Abhishek Banerjee has sought the immediate sacking of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
WHAT HAS THE REPORT SAID ON BENGAL SIR?
To understand what the Indian Express investigation found, we need to look at the numbers first.
Around 90 lakh voters, around 11.60%, were erased after the Bengal SIR. A massive 60 lakh voters were placed under adjudication because of "logical discrepancies". After adjudication by judicial officers, roughly 32.68 lakh were found eligible, while 27.16 lakh names were ordered to be deleted.
Last week, the Election Commission told the Supreme Court that 38 lakh appeals were pending before the tribunals. These include 22.21 lakh appeals filed by deleted voters seeking restoration of their names.
The interesting bit is about the other 16.10 lakh appeals. These appeals were filed against voters whose names were retained by the judicial officers for inclusion in the rolls. These appeals sought their deletion.
Now, the Election Commission did not clarify who had filed these 16.10 lakh appeals. This was questioned by Election Commissioner Sandhu, as per the Express report.
In August, Sandhu wrote to ECI officials seeking to know who had been authorised to file these appeals on behalf of the poll body. In a note, seen by Express, he recorded that neither of the Election Commissioners (the other being Vivek Joshi), nor the Bengal CEO, was informed of the filing of the appeals.
"Who was authorised to file these appeals on behalf of ECI, and by whom?" Sandhu sought to know. "Who actually filed these appeals on behalf of ECI?" he further said.
Importantly, the Express report said these objections were also copied to CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
WHY THIS MATTERS?
The issue is significant because the Election Commission's 'Transaction of Business Rules' emphasise unanimity in decision-making. In simple terms, important decisions of the three-member poll panel are expected to be taken collectively.
Sandhu's note indicates that the Election Commissioners were kept in the dark on the filing of appeals.
WHAT IS THE ROW OVER ECI'S VOTER SOFTWARE?
Another major issue raised in the Express report pertains to access to the poll body's software, ERONET, by state-level election officials. This is part of the ECI's umbrella software ECINet, which was launched in January to bring all portals under one roof.
Basically, the software allows state Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to add or delete names and update voter records. According to the Express report, in May, the two Election Commissioners flagged complaints by EROs that they were being restricted from accessing the portal.
The portal is overseen by the Election Commission's Director General of IT, Seema Khanna. This issue was raised by Sandhu in August as well

items.title: Invasion coming? Panicked Pak readies hospitals, walls off Islamabad before PTI march
items.summary: Invasion coming Panicked Pak readies hospitals walls off Islamabad before PTI march
items.body_text:
Invasion coming? Panicked Pak readies hospitals, walls off Islamabad before PTI march
A panicked Islamabad is sealing roads with spiked barricades, deploying Rangers and creating space in hospitals for mass casualties ahead of the PTI's protest. The Jamaat-e-Islami has backed the PTI's protest seeking the release of Imran Khan, and farmers too will be marching towards Pakistan's capital.
Pakistan's capital, Islamabad, has been walled off with at least 20,000 shipping containers, welded together and fitted with outward-facing metal spikes, ahead of PTI's September 27 march demanding the release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan. Reports suggest that the establishment is panicking, creating space in hospitals and keeping additional blood bags ready. The march is being backed by the Jamaat-e-Islami and farmers organisations.
Hospitals in Islamabad, the capital, have been directed to prepare for a potential "humanitarian crisis" and "mass casualty incident". Non-essential surgeries are being postponed, and stable patients discharged to make space for a possible influx of casualties. According to Pakistani daily Dawn, Islamabad hospitals have been told to maintain reserves of at least 100 bags of blood and keep all ambulances and their drivers functional and ready for emergencies.
More than 20,000 police personnel are being brought from Punjab and Sindh to Islamabad ahead of the September 27 march. The Punjab government has called in the federal paramilitary force, Pakistan Rangers, in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali, reported BBC Urdu on Wednesday.
The mobilisation comes even as the Jamaat-e-Islami launched protests over soaring fuel prices, and backed the PTI march. Farmers too have announced plans to march on the capital, alongside the supporters of Imran Khan. At least two such bodies, the Kissan Ittehad Pakistan and the PTI's peasants wing, are planning protests.
According to Al Jazeera's Pakistan correspondent Kamal Hyder, many Pakistanis believe the government has "panicked" because it is unsure how large the protests converging on Islamabad could become.
So, Islamabad is bracing for multiple protest marches in the coming days. Commenting on the scale of the preparations, Pakistani daily Dawn said in a September 22 editorial, "Given the rate at which containers are being laid out, trenches being dug, and additional security requisitioned, it seems that the government is preparing not for a political event but an invasion."
To halt the advancing PTI supporters, the Asim Munir-led establishment has placed long lines of containers, which have repeatedly been used to block PTI marches into Islamabad. But, in previous marches, protesters have climbed over, pushed down and physically removed such barricades. This time, the establishment is welding containers together and filling them with sand and gravel to make them far harder to shift — elaborate preparations for a protest that the establishment's blue-eyed boy, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, has called the PTI's "drama."
The PTI's September 27 march has been called to demand Imran Khan's release from prison. Khan has been in jail since August 2023 and is currently serving a 14-year sentence in the Al-Qadir Trust land corruption case, one of more than 100 cases brought against him since his 2022 ouster.
Apart from Khan's release, the PTI has raised concerns over constitutional rights and the rule of law in Pakistan, where Asim Munir has amassed unprecedented powers, including command over all three armed forces and lifetime legal immunity, making him the de facto ruler of Pakistan.
The civilian government has said that it would not allow protesters to block roads or disrupt life in the capital. The Islamabad High Court has also ruled that political parties have no legal right to occupy roads, highways or other public places. items.title: If vote chori, how did we lose? BJP cites Bengal seats with most deletions
items.summary: If vote chori how did we lose BJP cites Bengal seats with most deletions
items.body_text:
If vote chori, how did we lose? BJP cites Bengal seats with most deletions
BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra hit back at the Opposition over the Election Commission's dissent report, asking how the BJP could have benefited from voter deletions when it lost more than half of the 20 Bengal seats with the most deletions. He also defended the EC's deliberations as part of the democratic process.
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) hit out at the Opposition over the row surrounding the Election Commission’s dissent report, arguing that the claim that voter deletions helped the BJP win the Bengal election does not hold up.
“The edifice is that because of the deletion of voters from the voter list, the BJP won in Bengal. The highest number of voters were deleted in 20 Assembly seats, of which the TMC won 13 and the BJP won six. If we won through ‘vote chori’, then how did we lose more than half of the seats?” BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra asked.
BJP QUESTIONS VOTER DELETION CLAIM
Patra cited the example of several seats, including Murshidabad’s Samserganj, where 91,712 voters -- more than one in three names -- were deleted from the electoral rolls after the SIR, the highest number of deletions from a single seat in Bengal.
Mohammed Noor Alam of the All India Trinamool Congress won the seat with 61,918 votes, defeating his closest rival from the Congress, while the BJP was nowhere in the picture.
Patra launched an all-out attack on the Opposition after the Election Commission responded to an Indian Express report that revealed that two of the three Election Commissioners had objected to several SIR processes, including those conducted during the recently concluded Bengal Assembly elections.
MAMATA DEMANDS BENGAL RE-ELECTION
As Patra defended the BJP, former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee launched a Facebook Live of her own, demanding fresh elections in Bengal and the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, while calling the Indian Express report “scandalous.”
"BJP and Gyanesh Kumar is a joint venture company. They together looted the Bengal election. If you have any moral strength, give back our election," Banerjee said.
ERONET AT THE CENTRE OF ROW
In Bengal, the Supreme Court did not leave the process of deciding the SIR appeals entirely in the hands of the poll body and instead handed the flagged voters over to 700 judicial officers.
The judicial officers eventually decided to delete 27 lakh voters and retain 33 lakh voters on the electoral rolls.
When the Election Commission appealed against the voters whom the judges had decided to retain on the rolls, lakhs of appeals were filed using ERONET. Most of these appeals were filed in the name of a single officer and through the same officer.
The software at the centre of the recent Election Commission row is ERONET, which is integrated into the poll body’s umbrella platform, ECINET. The software allows the process to be carried out at the click of a button.
When the Supreme Court asked the EC to account for these appeals, Election Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu wrote to his officers seeking details of who had authorised the appeals and who had filed them. He did not know, the Indian Express reported in its investigative report.
WE ARE SAVING DEMOCRACY: PATRA
Patra said Opposition parties had been rejected by people since 2014, after Prime Minister Narendra Modi came to power.
“You would remember that since 2014 after Modi ji came to power, all opposition political parties have been rejected by people,” he said.
He said the Congress began attacking constitutional institutions after realising that it could not win the hearts of people in India.
“When Congress party realised that it cannot win over the hearts of people of India, it started attacking constitutional institutions,” Patra said.
He accused the Opposition of repeatedly attacking the Election Commission of India.
“They have been attacking ECI. But now ECI has issued a detailed note,” he said.
On the dissent

items.title: J&K Assembly clash: BJP and NC fight over Maharaja Hari Singh and Sheikh Abdullah holidays
items.summary: Explore the political clash in the Jammu and Kashmir Assembly as the BJP and National Conference spar over public holidays for Maharaja Hari Singh and Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah. Get key insights into the heated debate, walkouts, and historical legacies.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah speaks during the Autumn Session of the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly in Srinagar. (IANS)
Confronting the NC in assembly and reacting sharply to the NC's stance on the ground BJP Jammu Kashmir unit leaders stated that there is no comparison whatsoever between Maharaja Hari Singh and Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah and first time in the history of the Jammu Kashmir BJP, they celebrated Maharaja Hari Singh's birthday today and explained his role, contributions, and stature in Jammu and Kashmir and said it was several times larger than Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, the grandfather of Chief Minister Omar Abdullah. The BJP stated it was Maharaja Hari Singh who played the monumental and historic role in formally merging Jammu and Kashmir with the Union of India.
BJP Jammu-Kashmir spokesperson Altaf Thakur said, "The Maharaja was a great personality, a great leader, and a great guide. When people in Kashmir were not even wearing shalwar-kameez or pajamas during the National Conference era, he emphasized education here, improved the health sector, brought development, and talked about women's empowerment. That is the difference. And today, you cannot compare Sheikh Abdullah and Maharaja. Look at all the big institutions this flood channel, SVS, SMHS, SP College, Jammu and Kashmir Bank—how big Maharaja's contribution is! And the biggest contribution Maharaja made was the accession, or merger, that he did with the Union of India, and today we are called the greatest democracy in the world because of Maharaja's vision. On the other hand, if Sheikh Abdullah is spoken of, cases like plebiscites and FIRs for anti-national activities were filed against him. You cannot compare these two people, and the holiday given in Maharaja's name today is even less. Because Maharaja's personality was such; he was a ruler of course, but more than that, he was a human being who served humanity.
If there should be a holiday for Sheikh Abdullah's birth or death anniversary, then what about Mir Sahib, Mufti Saeed Sahib, and other chief ministers who served here? Why not them? You cannot compare Maharaja and Sheikh Abdullah under any circumstances. Maharaja joined with India, while the National Conference and Sheikh Abdullah's policy was always to stay away from India and break away. Therefore, you cannot view these two personalities together.
The BJP championed the Maharaja as a truly secular ruler who treated all communities Hindus, Muslims, and Sikhs equally, noting that his popularity spanned across regions.
From pioneering infrastructure like the flood channels and medical institutes such as SMHS hospital, introducing state subjects, and launching the "land-to-the-tiller" reform, the Maharaja’s foundational developments continue to serve the people to this day. The BJP accused the National Conference of playing divisive politics and harboring a persistence against the enduring legacy of the Dogra ruler.
R S Pathaniya MLA BJP said, “Not just his birthday, but his ideology and his thoughts, such as what was said in India about "The Idea of India," and the idea of Jammu and Kashmir that those people gave, have found relevance today, several years after his passing. On behalf of myself and my party, I have offered floral tributes and my heartfelt respects to him today.
Some political parties and political elements, with their petty, narrow-minded, and narrow-hearted vision under a political lens, tried to blacken Maharaja Hari Singh’s name, paint his history and his era with a black brush, and create an atmosphere of uncertainty. But today, Jammu and Kashmir and the Government of India recognised and acknowledged that after a continuous struggle not just in Jammu but in Kashmir, Ladakh, and everywhere else, his birthday should be declared a holiday. items.title: UP man kills wife, 2 priests, took 3 children hostage shot dead in encounter
items.summary: A man allegedly shot his wife and two priests before taking his three children hostage in Azamgarh, where he and his son later died of their injuries during a police operation, officials said.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: X
A man who allegedly shot his wife and two priests before taking three children hostage in Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh on Tuesday was killed in a police encounter. During the standoff, the man also shot one of his children, a son. Both the man and his son were taken to a hospital, where they later died from their injuries, police said.
The incident began on Tuesday evening when the man, identified as Arvind Singh, returned home around 6 pm and found his wife, Babita Singh (32), performing a religious ritual with two priests, Mahendra Pathak (60) and Akhilesh Mishra (50).
A verbal altercation followed, after which Arvind allegedly pulled out his licensed gun and first shot his wife before opening fire on the two priests. He then took his three children hostage and locked himself inside a room with them.
According to Naveen Arora, Additional Director General of Police (ADG), Varanasi Zone, the police initially exercised restraint as Arvind refused to leave the house and insisted that they wait until morning. The situation escalated when Arvind opened fire from inside the house, prompting the police team to enter the premises.
#Azamgarh: थाना अहरौला क्षेत्रान्तर्गत ग्राम शम्भूपुर में एक व्यक्ति द्वारा अपनी पत्नी एवं 02 अन्य व्यक्तियों की गोली मारकर हत्या की घटना में वरिष्ठ अधिकारीगण द्वारा तत्काल घटनास्थल का निरीक्षण किया गया। आरोपी अरविंद को बच्चों सहित कमरे से बाहर निकालने के प्रयास के दौरान हुई… pic.twitter.com/JFcz1M94cu
— AZAMGARH POLICE (@azamgarhpolice) September 22, 2026
Police rescued all three children and immediately took them to a hospital for medical treatment.
"Arvind and his son died of their injuries during treatment," Dr Anil Kumar, Senior Superintendent of Police, Azamgarh, said.
#Azamgarh: थाना अहरौला क्षेत्रान्तर्गत ग्राम शम्भूपुर में एक व्यक्ति द्वारा अपनी पत्नी एवं 02 अन्य व्यक्तियों की गोली मारकर हत्या किए जाने की घटना पर पुलिस द्वारा तत्काल मौके पर पहुंचकर आरोपी अरविंद को बच्चों सहित कमरे से बाहर निकालने का प्रयास किया गया। पर्याप्त चेतावनी के… pic.twitter.com/6dGq3L7OSb
— AZAMGARH POLICE (@azamgarhpolice) September 23, 2026
Police are collecting evidence from the scene, while other necessary legal proceedings are also underway.
Arvind Was “mentally disturbed”
As per the police, Arvind’s mother and wife had previously raised complaints about his behaviour.
"After speaking with villagers, the accused's family members, and an individual who survived the shooting unharmed, the investigation so far has revealed that Arvind was mentally disturbed and exhibited aggressive behaviour," SSP Kumar said.
He further said, "His mother and wife had frequently complained about him assaulting family members and engaging in such conduct. Distressed by this situation, his mother and wife had organised a religious ritual. They suspected he was under the influence of an evil spirit and arranged the ceremony in the hope of dispelling it."
Arvind strongly objected to the religious ceremony and grew furious about it. When his wife remarked that he was insulting the priest performing the ritual, he became enraged and shot her along with two of the priests.
Local resident said, five priests had come to the house for the ceremony. Three managed to escape, while the other two were killed during the dispute.

items.title: IIT Bombay suicide case: Prof Suryanarayana Doolla sent on leave; questioning today
items.summary: IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla has been sent on leave and is expected to be questioned by the Mumbai Crime Branch in connection with the death of student Sahil Wakode, amid allegations of abetment to suicide and caste-based discrimination.
items.body_text:
Image Credit: IANS
IIT Bombay professor Suryanarayana Doolla, who has been named in connection with the alleged suicide of student Sahil Wakode, has been sent on leave while an investigation continues, sources said on Wednesday.
A case has been registered against Doolla on charges including abetment to suicide and caste-based discrimination following Wakode’s death.
Wakode, a second-year B.Tech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found hanging in his hostel room on the Powai campus on the evening of September 18. The incident occurred hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination.
Doolla, who teaches in the same department and was reportedly serving as an invigilator during the examination, informed the institute authorities about the alleged use of a mobile phone in accordance with established procedures.
Initial reports suggested that Wakode had used his mobile phone to upload the examination question paper to an artificial intelligence platform. However, the institute later withdrew from providing a detailed characterisation of the incident, stating that the matter was under investigation.
Meanwhile, the Mumbai Crime Branch is expected to question Doolla as part of its investigation into Wakode’s death. Officials said his statement has not yet been recorded, while investigators have already spoken to the student’s parents.
Wakode’s mother, Sonali Wakode, has alleged that her son informed the family he faced humiliation, abuse and caste-based harassment.
According to reports, she claimed that Wakode specifically named Professor Doolla and said the professor had made remarks about caste differences. She further stated that her son told the family this alleged behaviour had continued for about three months. These claims form part of the ongoing investigation and have not been independently verified.
The student’s parents have demanded Doolla’s immediate arrest in connection with their son’s death. Doolla had earlier been removed from his role as Dean of Students’ Welfare at IIT Bombay.
With inputs from IANS

items.title: Indian Express’ ‘ECI crisis’ bogey falls apart: How dissenting notes on SIR process were sensationalised and sold as ‘institutional collapse’
items.summary: Indian Express’ ‘ECI crisis’ narrative unravels under scrutiny, with dissenting notes presented as institutional collapse and sweeping centralisation claims contradicted by the ECI and ground-level EROs.
items.body_text:
If there is one thing The Indian Express appears to have discovered during its latest investigation into the Election Commission of India, it is that the words “internal crisis”, “illegal”, “centralisation” and “cloud over its conduct” make for excellent headlines.
Whether the evidence supports the dramatic narrative is another matter.
On September 23, The Indian Express, in a series of reports authored by Ritika Chopra, presented what it described as an unprecedented rupture within the Election Commission. Its principal finding was that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over 10 months on issues concerning the Special Intensive Revision, Form 6, electoral-roll software, voter additions and deletions and other administrative decisions.
The report then took those objections and constructed a much larger narrative around them: that powers were being centralised in Delhi, that statutory Electoral Registration Officers were being bypassed, that software was overriding field-level decisions and that the Election Commission was facing an unprecedented institutional breakdown.
There is just one problem.
The evidence presented by the newspaper does not automatically establish any of those conclusions.
And the Election Commission has now responded directly.
In a press note issued on September 23, the ECI said that it is a multi-member constitutional body and that written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances are standard features of its functioning.
Official Press Note pic.twitter.com/xIQvXHqMSt
— Election Commission of India (@ECISVEEP) September 23, 2026
It said operational queries raised during the draft stage are part of normal administrative practice and that differing views are a normal part of institutional deliberation before a final decision is taken.
That inconvenient fact substantially complicates the dramatic storyline being sold to readers.
An objection is not an institutional coup
Let us begin with the celebrated “14 objections”.
Yes, two Commissioners objected to various decisions. That is newsworthy. It is legitimate to examine what they objected to, why they objected and what happened subsequently.
But The Indian Express repeatedly moves from “two Commissioners objected” to “the Commission is in unprecedented rupture” as if the latter automatically follows from the former.
It does not.
The newspaper itself reports that the objections were made through internal notes and communications. In other words, these were precisely the mechanisms through which Commissioners are expected to raise concerns within an institution.
The ECI has now made the point explicitly: internal notes and observations are part of the checks and balances within the Commission. It also says that all official orders, decisions and administrative directions carry legal sanction and follow the statutory procedures prescribed under the 2023 Act.
In fact, the legal framework itself contemplates disagreement.
Section 18 of the 2023 Act provides for the Commission’s business to be transacted, as far as possible, unanimously, while providing for matters on which the Commissioners differ to be decided by majority.
So what exactly is being presented as evidence of institutional collapse?
The existence of disagreement in an institution whose governing law expressly provides for disagreement.
That may be an interesting institutional story. It is not, by itself, evidence of a constitutional breakdown.
‘Illegal’ according to whom?
The Form 6 controversy provides an even better example of the problem with the Indian Express framing.
The newspaper reports that the online Form 6 was modified to ask new voters whether they, their parents or grandparents appeared in the electoral roll from the previous SIR. It further reports that Commissioner Vivek Joshi had objected to the change and that Sukhbir Singh Sandhu subsequently described it as “unauthorised” and “ille

items.title: From donation appeal to charges of fraud: Who is Jay Singh Rathore, and how the revelation of an online scam is breaking the internet
items.summary: Jay Rathore stated, "Even Rs 10 or Rs 20 from people who are comfortable helping would mean a lot to us," for donations.
items.body_text:
A brother’s emotional appeal for his ailing sister moved people to donate, only for the heartwarming story to unravel as an online scam. A user identified as Ajayveer (Jay) Singh Rathore claimed that his 12-year-old sister was in danger of losing her vision and asked for modest contributions to help afford her medical care.
The post was made on X (formerly Twitter) on 21st September (Monday). He received over Rs 1.5 lakh from strangers online in less than a day following the request. He subsequently deleted the payment details, stating that the family had been offered more money than was needed.
However, concerns began surfacing in relation to the medical records in the post, and the story took a major twist. Shroff Eye Centre warned that someone had used its letterheads to fabricate a patient record, prescription and estimate. Afterwards, the discussion shifted from posts about funding to long X Spaces, where people confronted Jay.
How the story unfolded
Jay portrayed himself as a 16-year-old looking for assistance for his younger sister in the initial post, which has since been removed. According to him, her eyesight started to decline a few months ago, after which she was brought by her family to Dr Shroff’s Eye Hospital in Delhi.
The doctors determined that she had vitreous haemorrhage, an internal eye bleed that was impairing her eyesight, along with glaucoma. Jay wrote that although the family had already spent over Rs 2.5 lakh on her care, the subsequent procedure would require an additional Rs 1.2 lakh. He included pictures displaying an Aadhaar card belonging to a child born in 2013 in the post.
“Between our savings and help from relatives, we have managed to arrange Rs 50,000. We are still short by approximately Rs 73,000. I have attached the medical reports, hospital bills, cost estimate and appointment documents so that people can verify the situation. Even Rs 10 or Rs 20 from people who are comfortable helping would mean a lot to us. If you cannot contribute, simply sharing the post may help us reach someone who can,” he requested.
The Jay Singh Rathore (Ajayveer Singh) eye surgery donation scam is going to be remembered on X for a long time.
Scammers like this don’t just steal money—they erase trust. The real tragedy is that when genuine, desperate people ask for help next time, everyone will hesitate.… pic.twitter.com/q8zAGP0h5U
Jay further expressed that he and his sister currently reside with their father and grandma after their mother passed away during the COVID-19 pandemic. He stated that the family has limited financial resources because his father, who works in the fields, is their only source of income.
The appeal took off right away, as Rs 1,58,282 was given to him in just a few hours. He thanked everyone who had helped and included a screenshot of the money raised in a later update on X. He asked netizens to stop because the family had more than they required and deleted the posts that contained his payment information, remarking, “I’m genuinely overwhelmed by your kindness.”
