items.title: 'Drogômetro': novo aparelho que será usado nas blitzes da Lei Seca vai pegar motorista que toma remédio?
items.summary: Resolução recém-publicada pelo Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (Contran) prevê a possibilidade de fazer testes que detectam substâncias psicoativas, como maconha e cocaína, no organismo dos condutores. Entenda como fiscalização deve funcionar — e se pessoas que tomam remédios controlados precisam tomar alguma precaução.
items.body_text:
'Drogômetro': novo aparelho que será usado nas blitzes da Lei Seca vai pegar motorista que toma remédio?
  - Author, André Biernath
  - Role, Da BBC News Brasil em Londres
- Published
- Tempo de leitura: 6 min
Autoridades de trânsito brasileiras garantem que as novas regras para as blitzes da Lei Seca — que preveem o uso do "drogômetro", um aparelho que detecta o uso de substâncias psicoativas — não vão trazer nenhum prejuízo para motoristas que fazem uso de remédios prescritos por um profissional da saúde.
Essa dúvida surgiu a partir da publicação da Resolução 1.031/2026 pelo Conselho Nacional de Trânsito (Contran), órgão vinculado ao Ministério dos Transportes, em agosto.
Entre uma série de atualizações, o documento regulamenta os procedimentos de fiscalização e abre a possibilidade para o uso de testes capazes de identificar a presença de drogas, como maconha, cocaína, anfetaminas e opioides, no organismo do motorista.
Isso gerou uma certa preocupação entre condutores que fazem tratamentos com medicamentos que trazem algumas dessas substâncias em sua composição.
É o caso, por exemplo, de terapias contra a dor, que podem requerer o uso de opioides. Já alguns estimulantes usados no tratamento do transtorno de déficit de atenção e hiperatividade (TDAH) podem ser derivados de anfetaminas. E remédios com canabinoides também são utilizados para lidar com uma série de condições de saúde.
'Drogômetro': o que diz a nova resolução
Em entrevista à BBC News Brasil, Adrualdo Catão, secretário nacional de Trânsito, explica que a última resolução sobre o assunto havia sido publicada em 2013, e havia a necessidade de fazer atualizações.
"O objetivo da nova resolução e de toda Lei Seca não é criar situações em que o cidadão pode ser punido caso não use, ou faça uso regular (como em remédios, veja mais abaixo), dessas substâncias", esclarece ele.
"A lei diz claramente que não é crime ter (pequenos) vestígios dessas substâncias. Não é esse o problema, não é essa a infração."
Segundo ele, a infração é dirigir sob efeito de substâncias que podem afetar a capacidade psicomotora — o que representa um risco para o condutor, para os passageiros e para os demais indivíduos que estão por perto.
Ou seja: mesmo antes da resolução, já estava na lei que era uma infração conduzir um veículo sob efeito não apenas do álcool, mas de outras drogas que afetam os reflexos e a capacidade da pessoa fazer essa tarefa com segurança.
Mas, em breve, é possível que os agentes de trânsito tenham à disposição não apenas o popular "bafômetro", que avalia a presença de álcool no organismo, mas também o "drogômetro", que detecta o uso de psicoativos.
Essa tecnologia já é usada em outros lugares como Estados Unidos, Austrália e partes da Europa.
Como os 'drogômetros' funcionam?
Existem diferentes modelos, mas em linhas gerais esses dispositivos são um pouco diferentes do "bafômetro", em que basta assoprar num tubo plástico acoplado ao aparelho que faz a medição.
A tecnologia do drogômetro consegue detectar as substâncias psicoativas através da saliva.
"A amostra de saliva é coletada com um dispositivo bastante simples, basicamente uma esponjinha embebida em ácido cítrico", detalha o médico Alvaro Pulchinelli Jr., da Toxicologia Pardini, do Grupo Fleury.
O uso do ácido cítrico aqui, composto que aparece na laranja e no limão, por exemplo, serve pra estimular a produção de saliva e acelerar esse processo de coleta.
"A esponjinha então é colocada no aparelho e vai fazer a leitura do material coletado", complementa o especialista.
Nesse contexto, o uso da saliva é necessário por uma característica química das substâncias analisadas.
Ao contrário do álcool, que é volátil, evapora com facilidade e pode ser encontrado no "bafo" da pessoa, as moléculas de outras drogas não vão parar com tanta facilidade assim no ar que a gente expira.
No entanto, de acordo com a avaliação de Pulchinelli, a análise da saliva é um método muito mais cômodo e menos invasivo do que os exames que exigem

items.title: Houthis ameaçam atacar alvos dos EUA em caso de apoio à Arábia Saudita
items.summary: Os sauditas pediram apoio ao governo de Donald Trump para conter o avanço do grupo do Iêmen
items.body_text:
Mundo
Houthis ameaçam atacar alvos dos EUA em caso de apoio à Arábia Saudita
Os sauditas pediram apoio ao governo de Donald Trump para conter o avanço do grupo do Iêmen
Os houthis do Iêmen atacarão os interesses americanos na região se Washington apoiar a Arábia Saudita ou tentar uma intervenção no Estreito de Bab el-Mandeb, advertiu um conselheiro militar em entrevista à AFP.
O movimento pró-iraniano dos houthis tomou o controle no início do mês do estreito, porta de entrada para o Mar Vermelho, em combates que deixaram centenas de mortos. Também atacaram alvos sauditas, incluindo a capital, Riade, pela primeira vez em vários anos.
A Arábia Saudita, que apoia o governo do Iêmen reconhecido por boa parte da comunidade internacional, tenta conter o avanço e, segundo vários meios de comunicação, pediu ajuda militar aos Estados Unidos e a outros países para combater os houthis.
“Se os Estados Unidos ousarem intervir militarmente com suas frotas ou tentarem tomar o controle de Bab el-Mandeb, isto será uma linha vermelha para eles e para qualquer outro”, declarou Abed Mohamed al Thawr na terça-feira em Sanaa.
“Caso os Estados Unidos se arrisquem a apoiar a Arábia Saudita com ataques aéreos ou apoio aéreo (…), consideraremos como alvo qualquer interesse americano que se encontre ao nosso redor e não vamos descartar nada”, disse.
Ele acrescentou que os houthis fechariam Bab el-Mandeb “completamente para os navios americanos”.
O bloqueio imposto pelos houthis afeta o reino, principal exportador mundial de petróleo.
Os houthis afirmam que a Arábia Saudita executou centenas de ataques no Iêmen desde que os combates foram retomados em julho, o que, na prática, acabou com uma trégua de quatro anos.
A guerra civil no Iêmen ficou mais intensa com o conflito bélico deflagrado em fevereiro pelos Estados Unidos e por Israel contra o Irã, que respondeu com represálias contra as monarquias do Golfo e com o bloqueio do Estreito de Ormuz.
Thawr nega ter recebido instruções do Irã, mas afirma que são “uma aliança e um só corpo”.
“O Irã é um país amigo, aliado e irmão para nós, mas não nos dá ordens. Somos independentes em nossas decisões e em nossa soberania”, afirmou o conselheiro militar.
“Enquanto a Arábia Saudita insistir e continuar destruindo nosso país e atacando nosso povo, responderemos com mão de ferro”, afirmou Thawr.
“Temos capacidade suficiente para colocar a Arábia Saudita em seu devido lugar, puni-la e retirá-la do jogo nos campos do petróleo e da economia”, completou.
2026 já começou
Às vésperas das eleições de 2026, o País volta a encarar um ponto de inflexão: o futuro democrático está novamente em jogo.
A ameaça bolsonarista não foi derrotada, apenas recuou. No Congresso, forças conservadoras seguem ditando o ritmo. Lá fora, o avanço da extrema-direita e os conflitos em Gaza, no Irã e na Ucrânia agravam a instabilidade global.

Carol de Toni lidera; Carlos Bolsonaro e Amin brigam pela 2ª vaga: a disputa pelo Senado em SC, segundo o Paraná Pesquisas
O filho de Jair Bolsonaro trocou o Rio de Janeiro pelo estado da região Sul do país em busca de uma vaga na Casa Alta
O novo levantamento do Paraná Pesquisas sobre a disputa pelo Senado em Santa Catarina, publicado nesta quarta-feira 23, mostra briga aberta por uma das duas cadeiras destinadas ao estado. Enquanto Carol de Toni (PL) está na primeira posição, Carlos Bolsonaro (também do PL) e Esperidião Amin (PP) empatam na vice-liderança.

items.title: Canada reveals new rules for checking inbound visitors, visas
items.summary: Canada’s immigration department has revealed new operational details for its multi-layered screening system for visitors, using over 40 criteria. Read More: https://punchng.com/canada-reveals-new-rules-for-checking-inbound-visitors-visas/
items.body_text:
Canada’s immigration department has disclosed new operational details outlining the multi-layered screening system governing visitor entry into the country, confirming that more than 40 national policy criteria are used to evaluate country-level visa requirements amid surging global application volumes.
In a post on IRCC’s X handle on Wednesday, the details were published in Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada’s (IRCC) 2026 Deputy Minister transition briefing, highlighting a tighter, risk-based approach to border integrity as visitor applications are projected to reach approximately 5.8 million.
Macro-Level Policy vs. Individual Assessment
According to the briefing, Canada’s Visa Policy Framework relies on a broad set of over 40 national criteria to determine whether foreign citizens require a traditional visa or qualify for visa-exempt travel. Key policy factors include:
Safety and Security: Evaluating national risks and potential threats to public safety.
Document Integrity: Assessing the security and management of foreign passports.
Economic & Bilateral Factors: Weighing trade benefits, tourism, and diplomatic ties.
Migration Trends: Tracking asylum claim volumes and history of visa violations, including unauthorized work or study.
IRCC clarified that these 40-plus criteria apply strictly at the national policy level to dictate border access rules for entire countries. They do not function as a point-based checklist for evaluating individual travel applicants.
Case-by-Case Individual Screening
For individual applicants requiring a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV), immigration officers conduct manual, case-by-case assessments. Decisions are based on a range of personal indicators rather than fixed scoring thresholds:
Applicant Intent: Reviewing travel history, employment, and family ties to ensure the applicant intends to leave Canada upon visa expiration.
Financial Capacity: Verifying sufficient funds to cover the stay without establishing mandatory minimum account balances.
Admissibility Checks: Conducting health, criminal, and security evaluations. High-risk files may be referred to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) or the Canadian Security Intelligence Service (CSIS) for secondary screening.
Systemic Risk Tools and High-Volume Demand
To handle record volumes—led by high applicant demand from major source markets like India and China—IRCC has deployed macro-level integrity tools:
Global Risk Framework (GRF): Launched in late 2025, the GRF functions as an early-warning system to monitor global migration trends and flag integrity risks before backlogs develop.
Biometric Enrolment: Processing nearly 3.5 million biometric records annually across 166 overseas Visa Application Centres to verify identity against security and prior immigration databases.
IRCC emphasized that while screening mechanisms have tightened to combat misuse, Canada’s operational objective remains facilitating legitimate travel for genuine visitors contributing to the national economy.

items.title: Ekiti SUBEB distributes 20 vehicles to enhance primary school supervision
items.summary: The Ekiti State Universal Basic Education Board has distributed 20 vehicles to monitoring officers to enhance supervision and quality assurance in primary Read More: https://punchng.com/ekiti-subeb-distributes-20-vehicles-to-enhance-primary-school-supervision/
items.body_text:
The Ekiti State Universal Basic Education Board has distributed 20 operational vehicles to monitoring and evaluation officers across the 16 Local Government Education Authorities in the state to improve school supervision and quality assurance.
Ekiti SUBEB Chairman, Prof. Femi Akinwumi, said the initiative was a strategic investment in strengthening the monitoring, supervision and quality assurance of public primary schools across the state.
Akinwumi, who spoke in Ado Ekiti on Wednesday during the distribution, said, “The vehicles will enhance school supervision, data collection and timely reporting by monitoring and evaluation officers,” adding that the exercise was evidence of Governor Biodun Oyebanji’s commitment to providing the mobility required to improve security and education delivery.
He said, “The improved mobility will enable monitoring and evaluation officers to reach hard-to-access schools, monitor compliance with established standards and provide timely data for effective policy formulation.”
The SUBEB boss urged the beneficiaries to use the vehicles judiciously and maintain them properly to ensure their durability and effective utilisation.
The Permanent Secretary in the Board, Michael Omolayo, described the procurement and distribution of the vehicles as a demonstration of the commitment of the Oyebanji administration and SUBEB management to repositioning basic education for greater efficiency and improved outcomes.
Omolayo said, “Effective monitoring and evaluation remain central to quality assurance in the basic education sub-sector.”
He noted that inadequate logistics could hamper effective supervision, adding that the Board had provided field officers with the necessary operational tools to discharge their responsibilities effectively across public primary schools in the state.
Monitoring and evaluation officers play a key role in assessing school activities, checking compliance with education standards, gathering data and identifying areas requiring intervention.
Regular visits to schools are therefore important for ensuring that policies and programmes translate into improved teaching and learning conditions.
The Commissioner for Human Resources Management, Dr Olufunke Fajobi, said the initiative aligned with the administration’s human capital development agenda, commending the SUBEB chairman for prioritising staff welfare and operational efficiency.
Fajobi said an adequately equipped and motivated workforce was essential to improving learning outcomes.
Also, the Commissioner for Project Management, Kayode Adeoye, said the vehicles would facilitate effective monitoring of SUBEB projects, ensuring quality delivery, value for money and sustainability of interventions in schools.
In her remarks, the Executive Secretary of the Universal Basic Education Commission, Dr Aisha Garba, hailed Ekiti SUBEB for the initiative and reaffirmed UBEC’s commitment to continued collaboration with SUBEBs across the country.
Garba, who was represented by the UBEC State Coordinator, Tokunbo Olajubu, said Ekiti had remained a model in the effective utilisation of UBEC matching grants and the implementation of the commission’s programmes, assuring that UBEC would continue to support the state’s efforts to improve basic education.
The ceremony was attended by SUBEB board member, Alhaja Lateefat Arilewola; directors of the Board; Education Secretaries from the 16 LGEAs; Headmaster-Generals; and the beneficiary M&E officers.

items.summary: Governor Umo Eno urges unity as Akwa Ibom marks its 39th anniversary, highlighting his administration’s achievements in infrastructure, education, and heal Read More: https://punchng.com/akwa-ibom-at-39-eno-urges-unity-says-states-best-story-ahead/
items.body_text:
Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has said the best chapters of the state’s story are still ahead as the state marks its 39th anniversary.
Eno stated this on Wednesday in a statewide broadcast to commemorate the creation of the state on September 23, 1987.
The governor said 39 years of the state’s existence had been defined by faith, resilience, sacrifice, progress and God’s grace.
He said, “Thirty-nine years ago, our beloved Akwa Ibom State was born. Today, we stand together at 39. Thirty-nine years of faith, resilience, sacrifice, progress and God’s unfailing grace.”
Eno paid tribute to the forebears and past leaders who laid the foundation of the state, as well as traditional institutions, workers, farmers, teachers, clergy, professionals and entrepreneurs.
Reflecting on his three years in office, the governor said his administration’s ARISE Agenda was designed as a covenant of service to build, empower, protect and create opportunities for the people.
“My administration has undertaken, commissioned and continued work on more than 1,500 kilometres of roads and 43 bridges, deliberately taking infrastructure to rural communities. No community is too remote to matter. No citizen is too far away to be remembered,” he said.
On education, Eno said the state had sustained free and compulsory education at the primary and secondary levels, disbursed N1.69bn in bursaries, recruited 3,000 teachers and was transforming the College of Education, Afaha Nsit, into a university of education.
He announced full scholarships for two outstanding students: Uwakmfon Unwana Jacob, who received N30m to study software engineering at Nile University, Abuja, and Dr Joseph Akpan, the best graduating student in Medicine and Surgery at the University of Uyo, who received N160m to pursue a master’s degree in Surgical and Intervention Science at McGill University, Canada.
On healthcare, he said 258,000 people, including the elderly, had been enrolled in the state-run medical insurance scheme, while every local government area now had an ambulance service.
Eno said his government had supported more than 1,700 farmers with grants and inputs under the palm tree crop revolution and trained more than 4,000 youths at Ibom-LED and Dakkada Skills Acquisition Centre, with over N2bn disbursed.
The governor said more than 500 units of ARISE Compassionate Homes had been handed over to vulnerable citizens, while over N98bn of the N111bn in inherited gratuities and emoluments had been paid to retirees.
On aviation, the governor disclosed that the state had taken delivery of its fifth aircraft for Ibom Air, an Airbus A220-300, noting that the airline remained a symbol of confidence and enterprise.
He reaffirmed his commitment to the Ibom Deep Seaport project, describing it as a new economic gateway for trade, industry and jobs. He added that the state was investing in tourism assets, including the Arise Palm Resort, International Convention Centre and Arise Shopping City.
Eno also said the state had established the Akwa Ibom Electricity Regulatory Commission and Electrification Agency to improve power supply.
He urged Akwa Ibom people to protect the peace and unity of the state, saying political differences must not degenerate into hatred.
“Our peace is priceless. Our unity is priceless. Our brotherhood is priceless. Let us protect them,” he said.
The governor thanked Akwa Ibom people at home and in the diaspora for their support, assuring them that his administration would continue to build, empower and unite the state.

items.title: ICC convicts ex-CAR rebel leader for crimes against humanity
items.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday convicted former Central African Republic rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani on four counts of crimes against humanity, including torture and unlawful imprisonment. The 56-year-old was found guilty of overseeing beatings and other forms of mistreatment while serving as head of a detention unit during the Central African […] The post ICC convicts ex-CAR rebel leader for crimes against humanity appeared first on Vanguard News.
items.body_text:
The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday convicted former Central African Republic rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani on four counts of crimes against humanity, including torture and unlawful imprisonment.
The 56-year-old was found guilty of overseeing beatings and other forms of mistreatment while serving as head of a detention unit during the Central African Republic’s civil war in 2013.
Said, who was wearing a blue sweatshirt and jeans during the proceedings, reportedly shook his head several times as presiding Judge Miatta Maria Samba read out details of the crimes.
The ICC, however, acquitted him of three counts of war crimes.
Prosecutors had accused Said of presiding over the Central Office for the Repression of Banditry (OCRB) detention centre in the capital, Bangui, where prisoners were allegedly subjected to torture and severe deprivation.
The court will determine Said’s sentence at a later date.
The Central African Republic descended into civil war in 2013 after the mainly Muslim Seleka rebel coalition seized power, triggering widespread violence and reprisals between armed groups.
AFP

items.title: You are no match for Peter Obi, leave him alone, Awuzie tells Umahi, Soludo
items.summary: By Chidi Nkwopara OWERRI — Igbo leaders and the leadership of Ohanaeze Ndigbo have been urged to speak out against what has been described as continued attacks on the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, by some Igbo politicians. Former National President of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), […] The post You are no match for Peter Obi, leave him alone, Awuzie tells Umahi, Soludo appeared first on Vanguard News.
items.body_text:
Peter Obi
By Chidi Nkwopara
OWERRI — Igbo leaders and the leadership of Ohanaeze Ndigbo have been urged to speak out against what has been described as continued attacks on the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, by some Igbo politicians.
Former National President of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Prof. Ukachukwu Awuzie, made the call while speaking with newsmen in Owerri.
Awuzie specifically urged Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo and the Minister of Works, Engr. Dave Umahi, to focus on their respective responsibilities rather than attacking Obi’s record.
He also expressed concern over what he described as the continued silence or apparent indifference of Igbo leaders to the exchanges involving the politicians.
His words: “The patriotic Igbo man is known for speaking out. So, what are our Elders-in-Council in the South-East doing? What about those in Ohanaeze Ndigbo and those in Imeobi of Ohanaeze?
“Why can’t they call Governor Soludo and Engr. Umahi to order? They should tell the duo to leave Obi alone.”
Awuzie advised Soludo and Umahi to concentrate on their public responsibilities, saying attempts to discredit Obi’s record as governor would not succeed.
“There should be a limit to greed, envy and jealousy. They should face governance; govern well and minister well. They can’t be a match to Obi, no matter how they try to rubbish his credibility. Igbo elders should rise and show leadership,” he said.
The former ASUU president further described Obi as the kind of leader he believes Nigeria needs at the present time.
“Obi is a kind of leader Nigeria wants at this point in time. He is a different breed of politician. So, if Nigerians know what is good for them, they should bank on Mr. Peter Obi,” he said.
Awuzie also dismissed suggestions that comments by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his supporters could damage Obi’s reputation.
“No matter what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his stooges do or say, they will not succeed in putting a dent on the integrity, character and personality of Mr. Peter Obi,” he said.
He described Obi as a model and said he believed many Nigerians, beyond the South-East, were proud of him.
“Obi is a model and somebody Ndigbo are proud of and I believe that other Nigerians are also proud of him. This is because, wherever he goes across the country, people troop out to welcome him,” Awuzie added.

items.title: ‘I hope to dedicate Ballon d’Or to Africa if I win’ — Mbappe
items.summary: Mbappe is seeking the first Ballon d’Or of his career after another prolific season with Real Madrid and a standout FIFA World Cup with France. The post ‘I hope to dedicate Ballon d’Or to Africa if I win’ — Mbappe appeared first on Vanguard News.
items.body_text:
Mbappe
By Adegboyega Adeleye
France captain Kylian Mbappé says he hopes to dedicate the Ballon d’Or to Africa if he wins the prestigious individual award next month, stressing that he has never cut ties with his African roots.
The Real Madrid forward, whose father is Cameroonian and mother is of Algerian descent, made the remarks in an interview with RFI, saying his African upbringing remains an important part of his identity despite representing France throughout his football career.
“I’ve always had an upbringing steeped in African culture, even though I was born in France and did everything in France,” Mbappe said.
“I have never cut ties with my roots, my origins. It’s part of the values instilled in you.”
Mbappe has increasingly embraced his African roots publicly and visited Cameroon in July 2023, travelling to Yaounde before visiting Douala and Djebale, the island where his father’s family is from.
The visit also included trips to schools supported by his foundation and a meeting with Prime Minister Joseph Dion Ngu.
“I went back to Cameroon not long ago,” he told RFI. “I used to go there when I was little, I had an amazing time. Every time I go to Africa, I’m always welcomed so warmly, I feel the love from people.”
Despite his African heritage, Mbappe said there had never been any doubt about his decision to represent France.
“I was born in France, I am French, I did everything in France,” he said earlier this year. “I have Cameroonian and Algerian origins, but I grew up with French culture.”
With voting for the 2026 Ballon d’Or approaching, Mbappe is among the nominees for the men’s award and is hoping to receive support from across Africa. The winner will be crowned at a ceremony in London on October 26.
A victory would place him alongside Eusebio, George Weah, Zinedine Zidane, Karim Benzema and Ousmane Dembélé among players of African origin who have won the prize.
“First off, I thank them for the support over all these years,” he said. “I’ve always felt so loved every time I’ve set foot on the African continent. I think that, having African origins, it’s always a pleasure when people associate me with the Ballon d’Or.
“I thank them for everything and I hope to leave with the Ballon d’Or, and in one way or another, dedicate it to them.”
Mbappe is seeking the first Ballon d’Or of his career after another prolific season with Real Madrid and a standout FIFA World Cup with France.
He scored 25 goals to finish as La Liga’s leading scorer in 2025-26, added 15 in the Champions League and another two in the Copa del Rey, finishing the season with 42 goals in 44 appearances for Real Madrid.

items.summary: The Foreign Office (FO) announced on Wednesday that Lieutenant General (retired) Nauman Mahmood had been appointed as the first secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. “The government of Pakistan is pleased to announce the appointment of Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood, Hilal-i-Imtiaz (Military), (retired), as the first secretary general pursuant to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” the FO said in a handout, referring to the alliance’s initial name.
items.body_text:
The Foreign Office (FO) announced on Wednesday that Lieutenant General (retired) Nauman Mahmood had been appointed as the first secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.
“The government of Pakistan is pleased to announce the appointment of Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood, Hilal-i-Imtiaz (Military), (retired), as the first secretary general pursuant to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement,” the FO said in a handout, referring to the alliance’s initial name.
“The secretary general will lead the general secretariat of the alliance being established at Riyadh,” the FO said.
The agreement — signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye on August 7 — empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all.
Its inaugural meeting was held on Aug 31, where officials from all member states met in Istanbul to establish the institutional structure of the alliance and Pakistan was picked to head its secretariat in Riyadh.
Under the decisions taken during the meeting, a secretariat headed by a secretary general will be established in Saudi Arabia to support the alliance’s work under the agreement. The secretariat will initially be headed by a secretary general from Pakistan for three years.
The three countries also agreed to take steps to further institutionalise their cooperation in a manner that would enhance their solidarity, ensure the credibility and effectiveness of their collective deterrence and defence, and contribute to regional efforts and cooperative security towards a just, inclusive and lasting peace.
Since its signing, there has been conversation about the possibility of its expansion, with Turkiye initially suggesting the possibility of Egypt’s inclusion. Though there has been no confirmation from Cairo.
From Pakistan, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar clarified soon after the signing that the pact was defensive in nature, with the latter saying that it was also “open to any country in the region” willing to uphold its fundamental principles.
However, when Foreign Office spokesperson Sajjad Haider Khan was asked about possibility of the pact’s expansion during a weekly media briefing on Sept 10, he said an expansion was not on the cards at that point.
The three countries first needed to solidify the new organisation before considering opening it to other states with similar threat perceptions and requirements, he explained.
Meanwhile, Inter-Services Public Relations Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said last week that the alliance has no “regional aspirations”, adding that it was intended for collective deterrence.
Meanwhile, as the US-Iran conflict continues to expand with Yemen’s Houthi rebels attacking Saudi Arabia, he also said that Pakistan would go to “any extent” to defend Saudi Arabia, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security was “unconditional”.

items.body_text:
The armed forces on Wednesday shot down eight drones launched by the Afghan Taliban after they entered Pakistani airspace near the Torkham border and Kohat, according to security sources.
The sources said the drones were intercepted by the air defence systems, which they described as “active and vigilant”.
“The armed forces and the ‘Shaheens’ of the Pakistan Air Force professionally thwarted the Afghan Taliban regime’s cowardly attempt to target public areas,” security sources said.
According to the sources, four of the eight drones were shot down in areas adjacent to the Torkham border, while the remaining four were downed near Kohat.
Earlier, security sources said two “rudimentary” drones had been brought down using “soft skill” methods about seven kilometres from Kohat city. They said the armed forces’ air defence systems remained on round-the-clock alert and were maintaining vigilance against “all threats from Kharjistan”.
“This incursion serves as yet another proof of the Afghan Taliban regime’s direct support and patronage of terrorists,” security sources said.
Later, security sources said the wreckage of the destroyed drones was being recovered. Last night’s exchange of fire in Kurram sector and Wednesday’s drone incursion “demonstrated the state of the Afghan Taliban’s panic and disarray,” security sources added.
The development comes two days after Pakistan, in response to recent terrorist attacks in KP, conducted “calibrated” airstrikes in the border region with Afghanistan against terrorist hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations.
A statement from the information ministry on Monday said that over 28 terrorists were eliminated in the strikes. “It is a matter of grave concern that Afghanistan continues to remain a hub of terrorism,” the ministry said at the time, specifying that the “threat to Pakistan emanates from Afghanistan”.
Before the airstrikes, security forces conducted a “well-planned intelligence-based ground operation” on September 20 against a group of terrorists in KP’s Kohat and Hangu districts, the ministry said. Nine terrorists were eliminated in the engagement.
The airstrikes came after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.
It should also be mentioned that on Sept 20, two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were eliminated during a fire exchange between a security forces convoy and armed combatants in Hangu, the military’s media wing said.
In July, the Afghan Taliban regime launched four rudimentary drones across the border into Balochistan, which were shot down by security forces. Two drones were also shot down in June in Qila Abdullah and Chagai districts.
Pak-Afghan ties
Tensions between Islamabad and Kabul have remained high, punctuated by cross-border clashes over the past year.
Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.
A day earlier, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar addressed a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and called for steps towards concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan.
Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional and international peace and security.
Last week, Pakistan also told the UN Security Council that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law.

items.body_text:
The Punjab government has requested the federal government to deploy Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali districts from Sept 22 to Oct 5 to assist the provincial police in maintaining law and order amid an expected protest on Sept 27.
The request comes as the Kissan Ittehad and PTI have announced long marches and sit-ins in Islamabad in the coming week.
PTI has announced a long march on Sept 27 to press for the release of its founder, Imran Khan.
The letter, a copy of which is available with Dawn, said Rangers had been requested for deployment in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali from Sept 22 to Oct 5.
According to a letter sent by the Punjab Home Department to the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control, three companies of the Pakistan Rangers have been sought for deployment in Rawalpindi, including one for Rawalpindi city and two for Taxila.
Five Rangers wings have been sought for Attock, while Jhelum and Mianwali have each been allocated one company.
The deployment is proposed under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1973, Sections 4 and 5 of the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, and Sections 7(b) and 10 of the Pakistan Rangers Ordinance, 1959.
The letter said the matter was discussed threadbare at the 59th meeting of the Standing Committee of the Cabinet on Law & Order (SCCLO) of the Punjab government, held on Sept 20.
The meeting considered the situational review presented by police authorities, the orders of the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in Writ Petition No. 4421/2026, and instructions issued by the S&GAD, Government of Punjab, through a letter dated Sept 19, 2026, it stated.
“After due consideration, it was authorised that the requisition be sent to the ministry of interior, for requisition of troops ensuring law and order in the districts mentioned above,” the letter stated.
The letter asked the ministry to take further necessary action and intimate the Punjab Home Department accordingly.
Section 144 declared
Separately, Section 144 has been enforced across Punjab from Sept 23 to Oct 5, with a complete ban imposed on the assembly, processions, or gathering of five or more people in public places, on highways, or in open spaces across Punjab. Inciting people to unlawful assembly is also prohibited.
The ban does not apply, however, to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, or gatherings at mosques and other places of worship. Courts of law, government or semi-governmental organisations’ official duties, and events held with official permission from the deputy commissioner of the concerned district are also exempt.
A complete ban has also been imposed on carrying or displaying weapons of any kind in public places, according to an order issued by the Punjab Home Department. This ban exempts personnel of law enforcement agencies (LEAs), intelligence agencies (IAs) and security agencies on official duty.
The order, a copy of which is available with Dawn, said that Section 144 was imposed in view of serious threats to public peace, tranquility, and the lives and property of citizens across Punjab.
“Multiple threat alerts have been received from IAs regarding possible terrorist activities being planned by such hostile agencies by employing suicide bombers, Vehicle Bound Improvised Explosive Devises (VBIEDs) and target killings during large public gatherings across Punjab to create mayhem, social unrest and disrupt public peace and tranquility,” it said, noting that “gatherings, rallies, public meetings, sit-ins, processions, and demonstrations” could become potential soft targets for terrorist attacks.
The order has been enforced immediately and is to remain in effect for 13 days.
The department has also sent a letter to the interior ministry requesting mobile and internet services at specific locations in Rawalpindi and Attock to be downgraded or jammed from the morning of Sept 27.

items.title: With reconstruction stalled, Gazans shelter in buildings at risk of collapse
items.body_text:
With reconstruction stalled, Gazans shelter in buildings at risk of collapse
- By AFP -
- Sep 23, 2026
In her Gaza City apartment, Heba Arafat walks uphill across a living room slanted at a steep angle after Israeli airstrikes caused the building’s foundations to collapse, leaving the entire structure tilted.
Like thousands of people in Gaza, Arafat chose to risk living in an apartment building damaged during nearly three years of war between Israel and Hamas, with countless Israeli airstrikes on the Palestinian territory.
“We were forced to live here because we had nowhere else to go. All of our homes were destroyed, our land was razed and we have nothing left,” said Arafat, 47.
According to the UN, 84 percent of all structures in Gaza had been damaged or destroyed by October 2025, and Gaza’s civil defence says 2,000 buildings across the territory are at risk of collapse.
Last week, 21 people including 12 children died in Gaza City after a six-storey building that local authorities said had been hit repeatedly by Israeli airstrikes collapsed. Israel denied having struck the building.
Arafat lives with her six daughters and husband in their old apartment building in Gaza City’s Al-Shati Refugee Camp, which they left at the height of the war that began in October 2023 with Hamas’s massive attack on Israel.
The family returned after an October 2025 ceasefire, which has reduced but not ended Israeli strikes. They found that their four-storey building, in which 30 people now live, had collapsed inward at the ground floor, the result, she said, of an Israeli ground operation in the area.
Like most buildings in Gaza City, the windows were blown away by blasts, with makeshift bedsheets spread across the frames providing little privacy.
As she spoke, Arafat illustrated her building’s slant by leaving a water bottle sideways on the floor, only for it to quickly roll away to the other end of the room.
While no territory-wide estimate exists, Ramiz Alakbarov, the UN humanitarian coordinator for the Palestinian territories, said last week that people across Gaza were living in “hundreds of damaged and unsafe shelters”.
‘Where can we go?’
“Where can we go? Even though this house is dangerous,” Arafat said. “We have been terrified ever since we heard about houses collapsing. The danger has become even greater” than we thought.
Gaza City municipal staff patrol the streets to identify buildings at risk of collapse and mark them with stencils.
“These homes pose a genuine threat to the lives of the displaced persons sheltering inside them, as well as to residents in the vicinity and those in nearby displacement camps,” said Hosni Muhanna, a Gaza City spokesman.
But Muhanna knows that people are likely to remain in these buildings for lack of better options.
“Thousands of displaced people are forced to seek shelter in these dilapidated buildings which are on the verge of collapse to escape the hardships of displacement camps that offer no protection against the summer heat or winter cold.”
Most residents of Gaza were displaced at least once during the war, and many of them remain in enormous camps for the displaced, in tents provided by humanitarian organisations or in improvised shelters.
Stalled reconstruction
With diseases such as the skin infection impetigo rampaging through certain camps due to the lack of waste disposal and general overcrowding, many Gaza residents have found it safer to take the risks of moving into the damaged buildings.
And with Gaza’s economy in tatters, many remain dependent on aid, which Israel has allowed into Gaza with restrictions since the declaration of the US-brokered ceasefire in October 2025.
But Israel has kept carrying out airstrikes, and has restricted the entry of a range of equipment that it says could also have military use, but which Gazans and international NGOs say are needed for the territory’s vast reconstruction needs.

items.title: Sophie Cunningham’s fame can ruin her basketball career?
items.body_text:
Sophie Cunningham’s fame can ruin her basketball career?
- By Web Desk -
- Sep 23, 2026
Sophie Cunningham is one of the most talked-about players in the WNBA these days. The Indiana Fever guard is known around the league for her scoring punch as a three-point shooter and energy off the bench.
But one prominent beat writer has noted that Cunningham’s commanding TV presence could ultimately cut her professional basketball career short.
Taking to The Robin Lundberg Channel, veteran sports journalist Robin Lundberg made a bold prediction about Cunningham’s fate at the Fever and the league.
” If I had to put money on it, Sophie Cunningham won’t be on the Indiana Fever next year and she might not be in the league next year. ” – Robin Lundberg
Lundberg flagged court time fluctuations after off-court comments as possible indicators. Cunningham’s court time had spiked after a public airing of her perceived intensity on the practice floor before plunging to just seven minutes in the following game – which happened to be the game in which coaching staff questioned defensive Concentrating and rebounding commitment.
Lundberg says sports teams want loud personalities, but front offices get frustrated when off-court podcast comments become more prominent than what happens on-court, especially when they’re made by role players.
Cunningham’s platform has grown rapidly:
2025: Co-hosted “Show Me Something” podcast with West Wilson.
September 2026: Re-launched the show “No Hesitation” with Drew Hanlen, a respected basketball trainer.
Her outspoken attitude and openness have caused a tidal wave of fans to lean forward in their seats, prompting outside analysts to suggest that Cunningham is trying to learn the ropes before she makes a smooth leap into broadcasting and digital media.
The On-Court Counterargument
Lundberg said, though, backing away from Cunningham wouldn’t be an easy decision for Indiana to make:
Metric / Aspect Performance Summary
Production off the Bench ~8.0 PPG
3-Point Efficiency 42.7% 3PT (Second highest mark of her career)
Standings by Teams Indiana Fever clinched a top-5 playoff seed
Locker Room Chemistry Good chemistry with teammates, such as Caitlin Clark
Even if media distractions can be limiting, Miller’s shooting and postseason playing experience will continue to be valuable for the Indiana Fever as they look to challenge for a title. Miller’s ability to produce either as a full-time media member or just to supplement her basketball career will be determined by Indiana’s postseason success.

items.title: Pakistan appoints first Secretary General of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
items.body_text:
Pakistan appoints first Secretary General of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
- By Laiq Ur Rehman -
- Sep 23, 2026
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan has appointed Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood (retd), Hilal-e-Imtiaz (Military), as the first Secretary General of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Wednesday.
According to the Office of the Spokesperson, the Government of Pakistan has appointed Lt Gen Nauman Mahmood as Secretary General pursuant to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement.
The Secretary General will lead the General Secretariat of the alliance, which is being established in Riyadh, the statement said.
The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye in Makkah on August 7, 2026. The agreement is aimed at strengthening collective security, defence cooperation and regional stability. It stipulates that an armed attack against any one of the three countries will be regarded as an attack against all three.
Read Also: Saudi Arabia resumes operations of East-West crude pipeline after drone strikes
The three countries agreed in August to establish a Secretariat in Saudi Arabia headed by a Secretary General, with Pakistan providing the first Secretary General for a three-year term.
The appointment comes amid heightened regional tensions.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated Pakistan’s strongest condemnation of recent Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed that Pakistan stood unwaveringly, shoulder to shoulder, with the Kingdom in safeguarding its security.
In his message on Saudi National Day, observed annually on September 23, the prime minister said any threat to the sanctity and security of the Haramain Sharifain deeply wounds the sentiments of Muslims around the world.
He referred to the recent attempted drone attack near the holy city of Makkah Al-Mukarramah. Saudi authorities said the drone was intercepted, while the Houthis have denied targeting Makkah.
Extending his warmest felicitations to King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and the people of Saudi Arabia, Shehbaz said the Kingdom’s remarkable journey of progress and transformation was a source of pride and admiration for both the Saudi and Pakistani peoples.
The prime minister, who is currently in New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, said that under the leadership of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Saudi Arabia continued to make impressive strides towards greater prosperity, modernisation and innovation.

items.body_text:
Iraq urges Iran to defuse regional tensions through dialogue
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized to his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, on Wednesday the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.
Hussein’s remarks took place during his meeting with Araghchi in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.
The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.
Hussein stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension, prevent escalation, and maintain regional stability.
Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.
The two sides discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.
The two ministers emphasized the importance of supporting diplomatic efforts aimed at preventing escalation, defusing tensions, and fostering opportunities for dialog and peaceful solutions.

items.title: China’s Yu, 13, wins third gold with latest Asian Games record
items.summary: China's 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds on Wednesday with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years... The post China’s Yu, 13, wins third gold with latest Asian Games record appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
China’s Yu, 13, wins third gold with latest Asian Games record
Tokyo – China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds on Wednesday with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics.
The school girl powered home in an Asian Games-record 4min 28.56sec to make it a clean sweep from her three individual events in Tokyo, following victories in the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, also in Games-record times.
She beat the previous 400m IM Games record set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014 by almost 4.5 seconds.
It was the fourth-fastest time in the world this year, with world record-holder Summer McIntosh owning the top three.
Yu is shaping up to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
She has been the talk of swimming since becoming the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze for China’s relay team aged just 12.
She also finished just outside the medals in fourth in three world individual events.
She has embellished her growing reputation this year, notably with a victory over multiple American Olympic champion Regan Smith in March.
She has dominated this week in Tokyo and gave another glimpse of her immense talent in the 400m IM.
Yu took the lead straight from the start and set off on a procession towards the finish line.
She finished 3.95sec clear of silver medallist Ke Wenxi of China, with Japan’s Mio Narita finishing third.
As well as international news headlines, her Asian Games exploits have caused a sensation back home.
Her back story, such as being spotted by chance by a swimming coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, have gone viral.
Asked if answering questions was the hardest part, she replied with a giggle this week: “Every time I just want to float off somewhere else.”

items.title: China’s Xi heads to US for talks with Trump: state media
items.summary: China's leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald... The post China’s Xi heads to US for talks with Trump: state media appeared first on Iraqi News.
items.body_text:
China’s Xi heads to US for talks with Trump: state media
Beijing – China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said.
The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade.
Xi “left Beijing by special plane”, accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Trump is due to personally meet Xi on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews, before their meetings on Thursday, according to the White House.
The US leader was greeted by China’s vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.
Xi and Peng will attend a ceremony at the White House on Thursday morning, which will include a military flyover.
The two leaders are due to hold talks and Trump is set to host Xi for a state dinner at the White House in the evening.
The visit will wrap up on Friday morning where the two presidential couples will have tea at the White House then visit the National Archives to round out the trip.
The White House said that the visit marks “a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries.”
But the meeting between the two leaders could touch on multiple points of tension, with Trump telling reporters that he will be “discussing almost everything” with Xi.
Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran — despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.
A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs.
The threat of war over the island of Taiwan — which China claims as its territory — looms large as well.
– Leverage –
Analysts, however, have tempered expectations by cautioning there might not be many concrete deals announced.
Preliminary talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, but released little in the way of detail.
Bessant said at the time that the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”
“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.
The son of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai made an appeal to Xi from Washington that his 78-year-old father be released.
Trump said in May, however, that he had discussed Lai’s fate with Xi and his release was unlikely.
But Beijing did release the founder of an underground church, Ezra Jin, after Trump raised his case with Xi.
China’s negotiating arsenal includes its dominance in the supply of rare earths, critical materials used for high-tech products that are vital to US manufacturers.
Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths.

Developed by local startup Raed Bots in partnership with Egypt’s Industrial Modernization Center, the robotic arm boasts an 80 percent local component ratio—a figure developers plan … The post Photos: Egypt introduces its first industrial robot built with 80% local components appeared first on Egypt I
items.body_text:
Egypt has officially debuted its first locally manufactured industrial robot, a key milestone in the country’s push to shift from importing technology to building automated factory systems at home.
Developed by local startup Raed Bots in partnership with Egypt’s Industrial Modernization Center, the robotic arm boasts an 80 percent local component ratio—a figure developers plan to increase to 90 percent once motor manufacturing is brought locally.
Unlike theoretical or lab-bound concepts, the robot has already landed its first real-world deployment: it is being integrated directly into packaging machinery operated by QB, a domestic manufacturing firm.
Real-world application
The robotic unit is tailored specifically for industrial packaging and automation on production lines.
Academic-industry pipeline
Raed Bots also partnered with Mansoura University’s Faculty of Engineering to supply educational variants of the robot for hands-on student training and research.
The bigger picture
 
Officials hope the rollout demonstrates that Egyptian-engineered hardware can reliably replace expensive foreign machinery, cutting import dependence while accelerating smart manufacturing across local factories.

items.body_text:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) revealed its weather forecast and temperature projections for the coming hours, announcing the onset of weather fluctuations alongside chances of rainfall across several governorates.
Unstable conditions will begin over several northern regions, according to weather maps, stretching from the Mediterranean coast to parts of the Nile Delta.
Despite the persistence of relatively hot and humid conditions, cold air currents in the upper atmosphere will collide with warm, humid air, generating a brief and localized state of instability.
The atmosphere will remain humid due to rain-bearing clouds forming over the region, heightening the feeling of heat.
Once this brief weather system passes, temperatures are expected to drop noticeably starting Friday and Saturday.
Rainfall map: Scattered thunderstorms expected Thursday
Regarding the rainfall map, random thunderclouds are expected to form starting early Thursday morning over the northwestern coast (from Matrouh to Alexandria).
By afternoon and late afternoon, convective thunderclouds will build, penetrating and expanding over the Delta governorates—namely Beheira, Monufiya, Sharqiya, Gharbiya, and Daqahliya—in addition to Kafr El-Sheikh, Damietta, and Port Said.
Rainfall across these areas is expected to be scattered.
The EMA outlines autumn 2026 forecast
The EMA outlined the expected weather features for the 2026 autumn season, which begins on Wednesday and will last for three months.
The Director-General of the Forecasting and Early Warning Center at the EMA, Mahmoud Shaheen, told Al-Masry Al-Youm that potential weather fluctuations are expected, as autumn weather maps shift rapidly according to changes in atmospheric pressure patterns and distributions.
Light to moderate rainfall is anticipated, with thunderclouds potentially developing over scattered areas of the northwestern coast and the Nile Delta, with some rain potentially reaching Greater Cairo.
The EMA confirmed that seasonal forecasts suggest rainfall amounts and temperatures during this autumn may be slightly above average climatic norms.
Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

items.body_text:
Three months on, citizens await answers after appealing disqualification from subsidies          
        During an evening visit this week to a subsidized grocery store in Giza, Mada Masr asked the employee at the counter about how customers have been affected since the government began cancelling citizens’ ration cards three months ago.
The store employee said around 200 people who used to get their subsidized goods from his shop have had their cards suspended.
He believed many of those customers had been wrongly disqualified from the system. They include families whose children are enrolled in private schools charging well below LE20,000 per year and people who once owned cars, but sold them long ago.
Yet, none of these customers have had their subsidies reinstated since the window for grievances opened July 14, he said.
The government began in June to suspend ration cards for hundreds of thousands of citizens under its new “social justice” eligibility criteria. But three months on, official state bodies have yet to give a definitive answer on when these appeals will be resolved.
This month, when Mada Masr tried to understand whether the grievance system was working, we heard a similar story repeated in conversations with people who work in or with the subsidy system, from the street level to municipal supply offices and governorate authorities. All of them said they had no idea when or how the government would start reviewing grievances and reinstating subsidies for those proven eligible. And most said that none of the citizens who had filed grievances had received a response, with one source citing “seven or eight” restorations at most.
The lack of response leaves the thousands who have filed grievances in limbo, prompting MPs to press the government not only for a clear decision, but also to ask whether there will be compensation for the monthslong wrongful suspensions that have left card holders without access to subsidies.
The confusion in the supply system exposes many families to mounting price pressures, especially as inflation spikes, leaving many uncertain about the future as the government transitions the entire commodities subsidy system to a cash assistance model that relies on digital credit allocations.
***
To verify whether any complainants have regained access to their subsidies, a Mada Masr correspondent went to a ration office in Giza and asked about the fate of appeals. Staff there said that, so far, not a single person who had filed a grievance has been reinstated into the system. The office could only check the status of a ration card and see how far it is in the appeal process.
Another ration office employee in Sohag, Zain al-Abideen, reiterated the same, saying that of the citizens he had helped to file grievances, not a single one was reinstated.
Mada Masr also spoke to Badawy Dabour, who works independently to support people submitting subsidy appeals in Qalyubiya. Dabour said he had helped a large number of people file grievances, but only seven or eight have had their cards restored.
Dabour also mentioned other cases of wrongful disqualification: people with old cars, or whose children aren’t enrolled in private schools.
While citizens wait for the results of their appeals, no government body has disclosed when they can expect a response.
In televised statements, Supply Minister Spokesperson Ahmed Kamal said in August that the grievance process happens in two stages, with citizens required to submit data first via the Digital Egypt platform or via post office branches that have been dedicated to supporting grievance requests. The second stage is going to a ration office with a statement confirming that they don’t own the assets for which they have been wrongfully disqualified.
Once cards are reactivated, he said, beneficiaries would get a text message notification. He said people would be returned to the system starting August 1, but did not say how long the review process would take.

items.title: What is left of Maspero after national broadcaster’s debt-for-assets swap?
items.summary: The move eliminates debts that Maspero has been racking up since the 1980s The post What is left of Maspero after national broadcaster’s debt-for-assets swap? first appeared on Mada Masr.
items.body_text:
What is left of Maspero after national broadcaster’s debt-for-assets swap?                    
                The National Broadcasting Authority — known by the name of its Downtown headquarters, Maspero — has been weighed down by debt for decades, borrowing heavily from the National Investment Bank (NIB) as it has struggled to maintain a leading role as state broadcaster and production house in a changing media scene, grappling initially with the move to satellite, and now to digital media.
All of that accumulated debt, worth a total of around LE139.7 billion, was settled at the end of August, in a single assets-for-debt swap, with the Planning Ministry announcing that the ownership of 44 assets, unused by the broadcasting authority and worth around LE18.06 billion, including land and buildings, would be transferred to the NIB.
What the assets are, how they were valued and what will happen to them going forward remains unclear. While sources speaking to Mada Masr pointed to some of the land assets that are owned by the company and indicated some of those included in the deal, they were not aware of how these lands will be leveraged for investment going forward.
The move, however, eliminates debts that Maspero has been racking up since the 1980s as the state has, simultaneously, withdrawn its investments from its traditional media vehicles and focused instead on United Media Services (UMS).
The ministry has said that the step was taken in line with a broader move to resolve the historical debts of government entities and authorities, part of what it called “the political leadership’s directives.”
In this light, the Maspero debt-for-assets swap marks a major step toward implementation of plans the prime minister announced at the beginning of the year to resolve the huge amount of government debt, leveraging state assets and land for investment to write off public borrowing as part of the continuing process of shaping President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s “New Republic.”
How was the deal announced?
The swap was announced on August 26 as part of a framework agreement signed by the Finance and Planning Ministers, with the heads of NIB and Maspero.
The Cabinet initially announced that the total debts were LE88.3 billion, with the Planning Ministry elaborating the following day to state that the total debts resolved amounted to LE139.7 billion, including LE51.4 billion that were written off entirely and that included accumulated interest and late-payment penalties owed by the broadcasting authority.
The remaining LE70.24 billion would be repaid by the state, according to the ministry, through the allocation of land to the bank, with the aim of increasing the bank’s asset base and enabling it to redeploy those assets in national projects that would create more jobs — something the ministry referred to as another form of government support for debt settlement.
The file was to be fully closed, the Planning Ministry stated, and the accumulation of any new late-payment penalties halted as of July 1 until completion of the settlement procedures.
What remains of Maspero?
A broadcaster, a senior specialist at the National Broadcasting Authority and a news program director, tell Mada Masr in separate statements that the debt settlement agreement remained unclear and that there was a lack of transparency over how the 44 plots of land belonging to Maspero were valued at LE18 billion.
The broadcaster and the director both believe that the government has not disclosed the size or locations of the relinquished land so as not to expose its unfair valuation.
According to the broadcaster, who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, the state allocated vast areas of land to the authority since the launch of state television in the 1960s to ensure strong transmission coverage in every region, with every governorate having at least one television transmission center.

Future of Egypt enters healthcare: Govt, military hospitals to serve tourist dollars                    
                In its first public move into the healthcare sector, the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority unveiled last week the launch of the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company.
According to reports announcing the authority’s participation in this year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, the company is chaired by Major General Khaled Oweida, the physician and former director of the Air Force Specialized Hospital, and is set to provide specialized medical services, training and research, digital and technological healthcare solutions, as well as medical tourism services.
In the first phase of its operations, the reports stated, the company will incorporate the International Medical Center and the Air Force Specialized Hospital, both of which are affiliated with the Armed Forces. The two facilities provide medical services to military personnel through the Armed Forces’ health insurance system, while also treating civilians for a fee or through contracts with the Universal Health Insurance system or other entities.
The company plans to expand gradually by bringing additional facilities and hospitals under its umbrella.
Future of Egypt also announced that the company was taking part in the exhibition, which was held from September 15 to 17, in order to “showcase its integrated medical system’s components and the range of specialties, services and advanced solutions it offers.”
Coverage of the exhibition focused on what media outlets described as the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company’s vision for developing medical tourism — mapping the international patient journey that runs from pre-travel consultations and case assessment, through travel, reception, accommodation and translation, to post-treatment follow-up.
According to media coverage, the company intends to pursue this by building a network of medical partners and tourism operators and establishing cooperation channels with entities involved in medical tourism and target markets.
Steps to foster a state vision for medical tourism date back to at least 2017, when Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly established the Supreme Committee for Medical Tourism by decree to be headed by the health minister. The decree set out several objectives, including implementing the medical tourism components of the Egypt Vision 2030, restoring the confidence of foreign patients, attracting Arab and foreign investment to establish projects serving medical tourism and involving civil society and the private sector.
During a committee meeting in December 2024, chaired by Madbuly, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the committee’s technical secretariat had begun preparing a unified national strategy for medical tourism. According to a Cabinet statement, the committee had contacted all relevant entities involved in health tourism in Egypt to solicit their proposals for the strategy.
At the same meeting, Madbuly said that it was agreed to establish a national council for medical tourism, with a technical secretariat tasked with following up on all matters related to this portfolio.
The council was established by a prime ministerial decree in June 2025. In its first meeting, chaired by the health minister, a proposal setting out criteria for service providers to join the national health tourism platform was reviewed. The providers included healthcare, hotel and hospitality, transportation and logistics services.
A senior Health Ministry official told Mada Masr on condition of anonymity that the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company is primarily focused on providing treatment to tourists: “[The company] is targeting Gulf nationals and foreign tourists in Egypt whose treatment costs are paid in dollars by international insurance companies.”

items.title: EFG Hermes Secures Top Corporate Access and Research Rankings in 2026 Extel Emerging EMEA Survey
items.summary: EFG Hermes, an EFG Holding company and the leading investment bank in the Middle East and North Africa, has secured leading positions in the 2026 Extel Emerging EMEA Research Survey, ranking No. 1 in the Corporate Access Conference category for the second consecutive year, while its Research division earned multiple top rankings across key sectors. […] The post EFG Hermes Secures Top Corporate Access and Research Rankings in 2026 Extel Emerging EMEA Survey first appeared on Dailynewsegypt.
items.body_text:
EFG Hermes, an EFG Holding company and the leading investment bank in the Middle East and North Africa, has secured leading positions in the 2026 Extel Emerging EMEA Research Survey, ranking No. 1 in the Corporate Access Conference category for the second consecutive year, while its Research division earned multiple top rankings across key sectors.
The results underscore EFG Hermes’ position as a leading platform for investment dialogue across MENA, combining best-in-class corporate access with deep sector expertise and high-quality research to connect global investors with the region’s most compelling opportunities.
EFG Hermes’ No. 1 ranking in Corporate Access Conferences reflects the continued strength of its flagship EFG Hermes One-on-One Conference, which remains the largest investment forum dedicated to MENA. The 19th edition hosted 220 companies from 12 countries and welcomed 675 institutional investors and fund managers representing 252 global institutions, reinforcing its role as a key meeting point for international capital, listed companies, and regional policymakers.
“This ranking reflects the scale, relevance, and execution strength of EFG Hermes’ corporate access platform,” said Mohmed Ebeid, Co-CEO of EFG Hermes, an EFG Holding company. “Being ranked No. 1 in Corporate Access Conferences for the second consecutive year is a clear vote of confidence from our clients and reinforces the role we play in bringing global and regional capital closer to MENA’s listed companies. As the region commands a larger share of emerging-market investor attention, access to management teams, policymakers, and sector leaders is critical. Our focus is to deliver that access with substance, consistency, and depth, enabling investors to make better-informed allocation decisions across MENA.”
Together with the London MENA Conference, the EFG Hermes One-on-One Conference has become a fixture in the regional investment calendar, bringing together global investors, senior executives, policymakers, and industry leaders to examine the trends, reforms, and opportunities shaping MENA markets.
EFG Hermes’ Research division also delivered a strong performance in this year’s survey, with several analysts recognized among the top performers in their sectors. Ahmed Hazem Maher, Managing Director, Head of Energy, Transport & Industrials, was ranked the top analyst in Utilities, second in Transportation, and runner-up in Oil & Gas. Ahmed Moataz, Director, Head of Healthcare and Insurance, ranked first in Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals. Mai Attia, Managing Director, Head of Real Estate & Construction, ranked third in Construction & Real Estate. Hatem Alaa, Managing Director, Deputy Head of Research and Head of the Consumer Sector, ranked third in Transportation and was named runner-up in the Consumer sector.
“This year’s Extel rankings reflect the dedication, talent, and analytical depth of our Research team,” said Ahmed Shams, Managing Director and Global Head of Research at EFG Hermes. “We are especially pleased to see our analysts recognized across a broad range of sectors, including multiple top rankings. These results reinforce EFG Hermes’ reputation as a trusted source of strategic insight and reflect the confidence that the global investment community continues to place in our research platform. They also speak to the collaborative, client-first culture that drives our team and underpins the value we deliver to investors.”
The latest rankings further strengthen EFG Hermes’ standing as a trusted partner to the global investment community, with an integrated platform that combines market-leading corporate access, differentiated research, and deep regional expertise to help investors assess and navigate opportunities across MENA.
The achievements were celebrated at the Extel Europe & Emerging EMEA Equities Awards Dinner & Ceremony in London on 17 September.

items.title: NVIDIA highlights growth of Egypt’s AI startup ecosystem
items.summary: NVIDIA, American multinational technology company, brought together technology companies, startups, developers, investors, and academia in Cairo to discuss the development of Egypt’s artificial intelligence ecosystem and opportunities to deploy AI across various sectors. The NVIDIA AI Ecosystem Reception, held in partnership with RiseUp, comes as more than 200 Egyptian startups are enrolled in NVIDIA’s global […] The post NVIDIA highlights growth of Egypt’s AI startup ecosystem first appeared on
items.body_text:
NVIDIA, American multinational technology company, brought together technology companies, startups, developers, investors, and academia in Cairo to discuss the development of Egypt’s artificial intelligence ecosystem and opportunities to deploy AI across various sectors.
The NVIDIA AI Ecosystem Reception, held in partnership with RiseUp, comes as more than 200 Egyptian startups are enrolled in NVIDIA’s global Inception programme, while the company said its developer community in Egypt exceeds 46,000.
The event also highlighted an upcoming strategic partnership between NVIDIA and the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), aimed at supporting Egyptian startups and technology talent and developing local AI applications.
Paolo Guglielmini, Vice President of NVIDIA for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA), said Egypt has significant potential to expand its AI ecosystem, citing its large engineering and talent base and around 40,000 STEM graduates entering the workforce each year.
“AI development does not solely rely on investments or the availability of GPUs; it requires developers and talent capable of understanding challenges and deploying the right tools to turn them into practical solutions,” Guglielmini said.
He identified six layers needed to build a sustainable AI economy: talent, energy, infrastructure, chips, models, and applications.
Guglielmini also said that adapting AI models to specific business contexts, data, and operational challenges presents commercial opportunities for Egyptian developers and software companies.
The event featured AI applications developed by Egyptian startups, including AvidBeam, which works on AI-powered video analytics; Proteinea, which develops biological AI applications for protein design and healthcare; CyberFuse, which focuses on AI-enabled cybersecurity; and Marses Robotics, which develops autonomous systems and robotics for industrial and field applications.
Ahmed El-Zaher, CEO of ITIDA, said Egypt’s main strengths include its human capital and startup ecosystem, noting that local companies have developed AI applications despite constraints related to access to high-performance computing resources.
Speaking on behalf of the Minister of Communications and Information Technology, El-Zaher said ITIDA is preparing to collaborate with NVIDIA as a strategic partner to support the wider technology ecosystem.
He said the cooperation could help strengthen the capabilities of Egyptian startups and talent and support applications including large language models and speech-processing technologies.
“The transition of companies towards AI-driven business models is a promising area we look forward to leading,” El-Zaher said, adding that ITIDA is ready to work with NVIDIA to expand local talent and applications.
Layla Hassan, Managing Partner at Algebra Ventures, said AI alone does not constitute a sustainable competitive advantage for startups, pointing instead to domain expertise, proprietary data, and network effects as important factors in building defensible businesses.
Mohamed Elkerdawy, Chief AI Officer at Proteinea, said the company is developing AI-powered products aimed at addressing real-world challenges and is seeking to expand into global markets.
The event also included a presentation by Ahmed Mostafa, NVIDIA’s Regional AI Adoption Lead for the Middle East and Africa, on how developers can use NVIDIA software tools to accelerate AI development.
Startup executives also discussed practical applications of AI. Hany El-Gebaly, Founder and CEO of AvidBeam, said video analytics can be applied beyond security and surveillance to areas such as business intelligence, operational efficiency, and safety.
Mohamed Gebreel, Managing Director at CyberFuse, said the company is developing specialised AI solutions for cybersecurity, including a “cyber brain” designed to assist security analysts in investigating and responding to attacks while giving organisations greater control
