items.title: COA flags OVP over relief operations, documentation lapses
items.summary: In its consolidated audit report on the country's disaster risk reduction and management funds, state auditors reported that the OVP’s relief operations suffered from inconsistent reporting, unauthorized operational deviations, “issuance of open-ended mission orders,” and incomplete documentation.
items.body_text:
COA flags OVP over relief operations, documentation lapses
MANILA, Philippines — The Commission on Audit (COA) has flagged the Sara Duterte-led Office of the Vice President (OVP) over a series of control and documentation deficiencies in its disaster relief operations, raising concerns over the reliability and verifiability of its distribution records.
In its consolidated audit report on the country's disaster risk reduction and management funds for calendar year 2025, state auditors reported that the OVP’s relief operations suffered from inconsistent reporting, unauthorized operational deviations, “issuance of open-ended mission orders,” and incomplete documentation.
“Control and documentation deficiencies were observed in the implementation of Relief Operations, such as: (a) inconsistencies between Situational Report (SitReps) from the agencies/LGUs concerned and Office of the Vice President (OVP) SitReps; (b) deviations from approved Mission Orders during actual operations; (c) issuance of open-ended Mission Orders; (d) deficiencies in beneficiary documentation and distribution records; and (e) incomplete, missing, or non-submission of required documents, contrary to Section 9.0 of the Policy Manual on Disaster Operations Program dated June 26, 2024 and Section G of OVP Office Order No. 2025-74. These deficiencies reduced assurance on the completeness, reliability, and verifiability of relief distribution records and weakened controls over Relief Operations. (OVP).”
State auditors discovered significant discrepancies between the Situational Reports (SitReps) prepared by local government units or affected agencies and those drafted by the OVP. These inconsistencies involved welfare goods valued at P19.67 million.
The COA noted differences in the reported number of affected families, while some local reports completely lacked beneficiary counts.
“Although management attributed these to evolving disaster conditions and subsequent validation, supporting documents for the revisions were not consistently attached. Consequently, the reliability of the SitReps used as basis for planning relief operations and issuing Mission Orders was diminished,” the COA’s report read.
The COA also called out the OVP for deviating from its own approved Mission Orders during actual field deployments.
State auditors identified 24 relief operations, involving P39,009,054.98 worth of welfare goods, that altered schedules, distribution sites, and the volume of relief items and rice without securing documented approvals.
“The deviations included changes in schedules, distribution locations, quantities of relief items, and the amount of rice distributed. While management cited operational adjustments due to changing field conditions, the absence of documented approvals weakened assurance that the changes were properly authorized and supported,” the COA said.
Furthermore, the OVP issued eight open-ended Mission Orders for distributions totaling P84.12 million. Because these orders failed to specify target beneficiaries, auditors noted that the OVP lacked a concrete basis for determining the exact quantity of goods requested and distributed.
The audit further exposed widespread deficiencies in beneficiary documentation and distribution records.
State auditors also flagged uncertified Master Lists, unsigned Relief Distribution Sheets (RDS), duplicate entries, and incomplete beneficiary information.
In 11 relief operations involving more than 200 beneficiaries, the OVP inappropriately applied documentary requirements meant for individual crises rather than the procedures mandated by its Disaster Operations Policy Manual, leading to inconsistent practices and a lack of verifiability.
Compounding these issues, relief operations serving 33,980 beneficiaries and utilizing P25.27 million in welfare goods completely lacked vital pre-operation documents, such as verified Master Lists and SitReps.

Border gate police at Da Nang International Airport took under 30 minutes to trace the Chinese owner of a gold Rolex left at security screening.

items.title: 100-year-old seaside church is Vietnam's first climate change heritage site
items.summary: An abandoned church by Hai Ly Beach in the northern Vietnam's Ninh Binh Province, whose bell tower now stands next to the sea, has been recognized as a "climate change heritage tourism site."
items.body_text:
The century-old structure, which stands outside the current sea dike, is the Church of the Sacred Heart, which is associated with the birth and development of the former fishing village of Xuong Dien, now part of Hai Tien Commune.
It is known more commonly as Hai Ly church.
Xuong Dien was a coastal settlement in the late 17th and early 18th centuries. As people came to settle in the area, they built dikes and reclaimed land from the sea for agriculture and protecting their homes.
In 1885, the Ngo Ham Dike was built to a length of nearly 12 km, helping protect the reclaimed land.
But the place has been constantly affected by storms, waves, and coastal erosion. In 1925, the dike in Hai Ly Beach was breached for three kilometers. In 1990, around 1.5 km was destroyed and a new one had to be built 150 m inland.
By 2005, a 700 m section of the coastline in Xuong Dien was eroded.
Over the last century or so, the sea has swallowed almost a kilometer of coastal land in the area.
The Xuong Dien shoreline has retreated inland due to the combined effects of waves, currents, winds, and storms, with climate change being a contributing factor.
Managing tourism site
Now, authorities in Hai Tien Commune have been tasked with developing and managing the tourism site.
Associate Professor and Doctor of Science Vu Cao Minh, former deputy director of the Institute of Geological Sciences at the Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology, said the current location of the bell tower provides visible evidence of changes in the shoreline and the process by which people reclaimed and protected coastal land.
"The fact that a structure built about 100 years ago now stands on the beach, outside the dike, provides valuable material for studying the history of shoreline changes. It also shows how people have had to continuously reinforce dikes and protect land and production from the forces of nature."
He said the church is not just a relic but also important for its connection with the shoreline, dike, and history of human settlement.
He called it "a special type of heritage in Vietnam and rare in the world."
Internationally, structures affected by erosion, rising sea levels, and natural disasters are preserved for research, community education, and tourism.
In the U.K., for instance, the twin towers of the St Mary's Church in Kent have been preserved as a navigation landmark, and the surrounding ruins illustrate the effects of centuries of coastal erosion.
Minh said these models show that disaster heritage can become a valuable visual record if it is preserved, documented and appropriately developed.
"The value of a heritage site is not simply about preserving a structure, but about helping people understand why the structure is there, how the shoreline has changed and how people have responded. When this is achieved, the site can provide scientific, educational, and tourism benefits."
The area around the Hai Ly church includes Thinh Long Beach with its distinctive culture, cuisine, and fishing life.
Recognition as a tourism site will enable its development as a heritage site and the protection of the remaining structure, landscape, and records documenting changes to the shoreline.

items.summary: The Supreme Administrative Court has rejected an appeal by former prime minister Yingluck Shinawatra to retry the case that resulted in an order for her to pay 10 billion baht for losses from a rice-pledging scheme she oversaw more than a decade ago.
items.body_text:
The Supreme Administrative Court has rejected an appeal by former prime minister Yingluck Shinawatra to retry the case that resulted in an order for her to pay 10 billion baht for losses from a rice-pledging scheme she oversaw more than a decade ago.
The ruling on Wednesday affirmed the Central Administrative Court’s earlier refusal to accept a petition by Yingluck and her husband, Anusorn Amornchat, against the compensation order issued by the Ministry of Finance in 2016.
The higher court concluded that documents the couple submitted did not constitute new evidence capable of materially changing findings of negligence in the rice-pledging case.
As well, it said, the petition did not detail any factual error or procedural defect that could change the ruling.
The compensation order held Yingluck responsible, as prime minister and National Rice Policy Committee chair, for failing to prevent corruption and state losses from government-to-government rice sales in 2013.
Norawit Lalaeng, the lawyer for the former prime minister, said Wednesday’s ruling closes the book on attempts to get a retrial.
While the ruling appears to clear the way for the Ministry of Finance to enforce the compensation order, Mr Norawit said the legal team believed there were other grounds to continue challenging it, Thai media reported.
The Supreme Court’s Criminal Division for Persons Holding Political Positions found Yingluck guilty in 2017 of mishandling the rice subsidy scheme intended to improve farmers’ incomes.
Yingluck, who fled Thailand in 2017 before the court sentenced her to 5 years in prison, has consistently denied wrongdoing. Her legal team argued that the rice policy was well-intentioned and that she was not directly responsible for operational failures.

items.title: Bangkok tackles cable clutter ahead of IMF-World Bank meetings
items.summary: Bangkok is stepping up efforts to tackle its long-standing problem of tangled overhead power and communications cables ahead of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings next month.
items.body_text:
Bangkok is stepping up efforts to tackle its long-standing problem of tangled overhead power and communications cables ahead of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings next month.
The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) is working with the Metropolitan Electricity Authority, telecoms agencies and other partners to organise cables and gradually move them underground in key areas, Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said on Wednesday.
The efforts are aimed at improving orderliness, safety and appearances in Bangkok ahead of the meetings, which are expected to draw thousands of senior finance executives, central bankers and government officials from around the world.
Mr Chadchart said tangled communications cables had been a chronic problem in Bangkok for decades and could not be solved by any single agency because they involved several authorities and service providers.
An integrated approach was needed, including planning to move power and communications cables underground, organising existing cables and removing those no longer in use, he said.
Technicians from the Metropolitan Electricity Authority and telecommunications agencies join the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration in moving power and communications cables on Rama IV Road on Wednesday. (Photo: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration)
Three approaches
He divided the work into three approaches. The first involves moving power cables underground, removing electricity poles and relocating communications cables underground at the same time. This is considered the most effective, but requires considerable time and funding, so it will be carried out in areas that are ready and suitable.
The second involves placing communications cables in underground conduits where it is not yet possible to move all power cables underground. Existing underground conduit infrastructure will be used to organise large numbers of communications cables and reduce the number of cables strung from electricity poles.
The third approach, which can be carried out more quickly, involves organising communications cables on electricity poles by identifying and removing unused cables and reorganising those that remain in use.
Mr Chadchart said all three approaches would be used in other areas of the capital. He stressed that cooperation among all relevant agencies would be essential, as resolving the cable problem requires a coordinated and systematic effort.
The areas being prioritised for cable organisation and underground installation ahead of the IMF-World Bank meetings include Wireless (Withayu) Road, Rama IV Road, parts of Sathon Road and Lumpini Park.
Mr Chadchart said City Hall is also developing a system to prevent the problem of cable clutter from recurring. Agencies and service providers wishing to install new cables on power poles will have to follow the proper procedures and obtain the required permits or face legal action.
The 2026 annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group will take place from Oct 12 to 18 at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center. About 15,000 delegates and visitors are expected to attend the event, which Bangkok last hosted in 1992.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt speaks to reporters about City Hall’s work to tackle the decades-old problem of tangled overhead power and telecommunications cables. (Photo: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration)

items.title: Heavy rain likely across Thailand until weekend
items.summary: Isolated heavy to very heavy rain is forecast over Thailand until Sunday, according to the Meteorological Department, which has urged people to follow weather updates from official sources after an online panic over a “great flood”.
items.body_text:
Isolated heavy to very heavy rain is forecast over Thailand until Sunday, according to the Meteorological Department, which has urged people to follow weather updates from official sources after an online panic over a “great flood”.
An active low-pressure cell over Vietnam’s central coast is expected to move over the lower Northeast, East and Central Plains of Thailand, including Bangkok and vicinity, while the monsoon trough lies across upper Thailand, department director-general Sukanyanee Yavinchan said on Wednesday.
The southwest monsoon prevailing over the Andaman Sea, Thailand and the Gulf will also strengthen.
Accumulated rainfall during the period could cause flash floods, overflows and landslides, particularly along waterways near foothills and in low-lying areas.
Some provinces have experienced flooding on roads following continuous heavy downpours since Tuesday night.
According to the department, provinces at high risk of very heavy rain on Wednesday are Rayong, Chon Buri, Sa Kaeo, Chanthaburi, Trat and Bangkok and vicinity.
The video below shows flooding on a bypass road after heavy downpours in Muang district of the eastern province of Rayong on Tuesday night.
In Bangkok, governor Chadchart Sittipunt said he had ordered officials to regularly inspect areas prone to flooding since last week, including Sena Nikhom in Chatuchak district and Ram Inthra in Khan Na Yao district.
Officials have been working to ensure that no garbage is blocking drainage channels, while maintenance crews have been instructed to remain on standby, Mr Chadchart said.
Heavy rain fell across the capital around noon on Wednesday, leaving some roads inundated. Motorists were advised to drive carefully.
As for water flowing down from the North, Mr Chadchart said the current flow rate was about 1,500 cubic metres per second, which was not considered critical. However, close monitoring of riverside communities has been ordered.
Online alarm
Many internet users in Thailand were concerned on Tuesday after the online page “Tee Lom Fah Ar-kat”, which independently forecasts weather, warned of a “great flood” and predicted heavy rain “all day and night” for 120 hours.
The Facebook page, which has over 800,000 followers, was temporarily taken down. The same page recently had to apologise for spreading misinformation about an influx of imported Chinese chickens.
Ms Sukanyanee said on Wednesday that it was encouraging to see the public taking an interest in weather forecasts and preparing for weather-related conditions.
While weather forecasts have been circulating through various online pages and channels, she stressed that the public should rely primarily on information issued by government agencies for weather warnings and hazard alerts.
This would help ensure consistent communication and reduce confusion or unnecessary panic caused by information that may differ from official sources, Ms Sukanyanee said.

items.title: Xi Jinping heads to Washington for Trump talks amid US-China tensions
items.summary: BEIJING, Sept 23 — China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he wi...
items.body_text:
BEIJING, Sept 23 — China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said.
The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade.
Xi “left Beijing by special plane”, accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Trump is due to personally meet Xi on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews, before their meetings on Thursday, according to the White House.
The US leader was greeted by China’s vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.
Xi and Peng will attend a ceremony at the White House on Thursday morning, which will include a military flyover.
The two leaders are due to hold talks and Trump is set to host Xi for a state dinner at the White House in the evening.
The visit will wrap up on Friday morning where the two presidential couples will have tea at the White House then visit the National Archives to round out the trip.
The White House said that the visit marks “a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries.”
But the meeting between the two leaders could touch on multiple points of tension, with Trump telling reporters that he will be “discussing almost everything” with Xi.
Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran — despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.
A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs.
The threat of war over the island of Taiwan — which China claims as its territory — looms large as well.
Leverage
Analysts, however, have tempered expectations by cautioning there might not be many concrete deals announced.
Preliminary talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, but released little in the way of detail.
Bessant said at the time that the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”
“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.
The son of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai made an appeal to Xi from Washington that his 78-year-old father be released.
Trump said in May, however, that he had discussed Lai’s fate with Xi and his release was unlikely.
But Beijing did release the founder of an underground church, Ezra Jin, after Trump raised his case with Xi.
China’s negotiating arsenal includes its dominance in the supply of rare earths, critical materials used for high-tech products that are vital to US manufacturers.
Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths. — AFP

items.title: Iran airlines suspend more international flights as US sanctions take effect
items.summary: TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tigh...
items.body_text:
TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian airlines were forced to cancel some international flights on Wednesday after the US tightened sanctions on Iran’s aviation industry in a new effort to cripple its economy.
A travel agent in Tehran told AFP that flights to Baghdad, Muscat, Qatar, Georgia and Azerbaijan had all been suspended, but routes to multiple other destinations remained available, including China.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the new measures on Monday as part of an earlier threat to impose “economic D-Day” on Iran, an attempt to force it into submission following their nearly seven-month war.
But Iran’s aviation sector has already been a target of sanctions for years, and it remains unclear what the full impact will be and whether other countries will comply.
Even after the new sanctions took effect on Wednesday, a flight from Tehran operated by Mahan Air, one of Iran’s biggest carriers, landed in Guangzhou in China, according to tracking data from FlightRadar24.
China on Tuesday said it opposes the US sanctions and called them illegal. A flight to Shanghai was also due to depart on Wednesday, according to Tehran’s international airport.
Some flights to Istanbul were also scheduled, though others had been cancelled, the travel agent in Tehran told AFP.
“The situation is unstable and we are no longer selling tickets for the time being for fear of cancellations,” the the agent said, requesting anonymity.
A Mahan flight from Kabul was also expected to arrive in Tehran around midday. According to the website for Tehran’s international airport, other connections to Turkey and Armenia also remained possible using smaller Iranian airlines, including Varesh.
Flights to Najaf in Iraq and Dubai in the United Arab Emirates were also scheduled.
Bessent on Monday vowed to “shut down” Iranian carriers and punish anyone doing business with them.
“If they land, you cannot provide them with fuel, you cannot provide them with landing services, you cannot sell them tickets or you will be knocked out of the dollar system,” he warned other countries.
The restrictions will further complicate the ability of Iranians to travel abroad or return to their country.
Pilgrims
Iranian media also reported cancellations, with the Tasnim news agency on Tuesday citing a civil aviation spokesman as saying that Baghdad and Muscat airports “will no longer accept” Iranian flights.
“Other international flights, including Istanbul, will operate as scheduled and as usual, and at present there are no problems with these flights,” Tasnim said.
According to Tasnim, Iran’s aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims.
In Iraq, while the government has not publicly announced plans to enforce the ban, several sources including a senior government official told AFP that Baghdad would comply with the US measures.
The prospect of a suspension of flights between the two countries has sparked concerns from some Iraqi travel agents.
In Najaf, home to one of the most revered Shia Muslim shrines, agent Haidar Shamaa said “most travel companies in the city depend on booking flights” to Iranian airports.
Several travel agencies said panicked clients were calling for updates and were considering switching to land routes, which would mean much longer journeys. — AFP

items.title: Indonesia identifies body of missing Anak Krakatau crew member, seven including journalists remain missing
items.summary: JAKARTA, Sept 23 — Indonesian police have identified a body found in Bengkulu as crew member Surakman, one of eigh...
items.body_text:
JAKARTA, Sept 23 — Indonesian police have identified a body found in Bengkulu as crew member Surakman, one of eight people, including five journalists, who went missing while covering the Anak Krakatau eruption earlier this month.
Seven people remain missing.
Banten Police Chief Inspector General Hengki said Surakman’s body was found on Enggano Island in Bengkulu province on September 12.
“Based on the DNA examination, the body found on Enggano Island, Bengkulu, was genetically identified as Surakman, a crew member of the speedboat,” he told a press conference at the Banten Police headquarters in Serang on Wednesday, which was streamed live.
The eight were aboard a speedboat that departed Carita in Banten’s Pandeglang district at about 2pm on September 7 for waters near Anak Krakatau.
They were travelling to cover the volcano’s eruption when contact with the boat was lost later that day.
The five missing journalists are Muhammad Bagus Khoirunnas of Antara news agency, Firdaus Wajidi of Anadolu Ajansi, Arie Basuki of Merdeka.com, Yudistiro Pranoto of iNews and freelance journalist Donal Husni.
The two remaining crew members are Warta and Heriyanto. — Bernama

items.title: Dutch look to Xavi to restore traditional football ethos
items.body_text:
Dutch look to Xavi to restore traditional football ethos
AMSTERDAM, Sept 23 : Dutch footballing philosophy has had a marked impact on the all-conquering success of Spain recently, but now that the Netherlands are looking to bolster their own fortunes they have turned to a Spanish World Cup winner for inspiration.
Former Barcelona midfielder and coach Xavi Hernandez has become the first foreigner in charge of the Dutch national team since the 1978 World Cup.
Xavi, who as a player won the World Cup in 2010 and two European Championships, debuts as coach on Thursday when the Dutch host Germany in Amsterdam and will have three more Nations League matches in the three-week international window.
The Netherlands have turned to him for a change in perspective after spells under Ronald Koeman and Louis van Gaal sparked much disquiet over the team’s tactics and playing philosophy. Both coaches were accused of abandoning traditional Dutch values around ball possession and attacking football and employing counter-attacks as their primary weapon.
Although Van Gaal took the team to the 2022 World Cup quarter-finals and Koeman the semis of Euro 2024, elimination in the round of 32 at this year’s World Cup was a major disappointment.
"It is about how we in the Netherlands want to play football," said former international Nigel de Jong, who, as technical director at the Dutch football association, recruited Xavi.
"That means playing dominantly and being attractive in a good way while doing so. Dominant does not always mean playing attacking football; we also want to be dominant defensively. By conceding fewer goals, we want to try to win matches."
Although the 46-year-old Xavi is a relatively inexperienced coach, the Dutch feel that as a player, he had much of what their side misses, in terms of technique, discipline and creativity.
BARCELONA INFLUENCE
He also showed during his coaching tenure at Barcelona, where he won La Liga in his first season in charge, the ideas the Dutch supporters want to see from their team.
"After the first meeting, I immediately felt like going out onto the pitch. New ideas and a new way of playing football. I think it is also good for the group," said midfielder Tijjani Reijnders.
Xavi, who has a four-year contract, told a press conference on Wednesday he felt the players had bought into his game model and philosophy, which he has described as revolving around possession, position, pressing, perception, and passion.
“You need possession to win the match," he said. "You need the right positions. When you lose the ball, you have to press. And you need perception to see what is happening around you and understand the game. But without passion, you cannot play football.”
But he was also clear that winning remains the end goal.
“I think there is definitely potential in this squad,” Xavi said.
(Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by xx)

items.title: Greece proposes European Spectrum Union to raise billions for EU budget from 6G mobile
items.body_text:
Greece proposes European Spectrum Union to raise billions for EU budget from 6G mobile
BRUSSELS, Sept 23 : Greece has proposed that European Union states should create a European Spectrum Union which could use some of the funds raised by future national sales of 6G mobile spectrum for technology investment, easing pressure on the bloc's budget.
"The potential initial financial scale could be around €12–15 billion," according to the proposal, developed by the chairman of euro zone finance ministers Kyriakos Pierrakakis and presented to EU ministers on Tuesday.
"At this stage, this is a planning assumption rather than an official valuation or forecast, and does not include any potential future contribution from selected 5G rights," it said.
If the idea is accepted by the 27 countries making up the EU, the money could help ease the problem of how to finance the EU's 2028-2034 budget, proposed at €2 trillion - the main source of financing for all of the EU's main policies.
Negotiations on the financing are tough, because the budget will have to deal with new challenges like more spending on defence and making Europe more competitive, while retaining most of the spending on old policies to support farming and cohesion.
Among other new financing options, rejected by some countries and supported by others, is using a share of the cash that EU governments get from selling CO2 emissions permits to companies and a share of the tax on goods imported into the EU that were made in countries where climate policies are weaker than in the EU.
Other options include a tax on non-collected e-waste, a share of the tobacco excise duty and an annual lump-sum contribution from large firms operating and selling in the EU.
Further proposals include a levy on extreme wealth, on digital services, online gambling and crypto asset capital gains. Ireland will now have to see which of these options, or a mix of them, has a chance to get unanimous support from all 27 EU countries by the next EU summit scheduled for October.

items.title: Juventus keeper Grabara undergoes knee surgery after ACL tear
items.body_text:
Juventus keeper Grabara undergoes knee surgery after ACL tear
Sept 23 : Juventus keeper Kamil Grabara has undergone knee surgery after tearing his anterior cruciate ligament during training, the 27-year-old announced on social media on Wednesday.
Grabara is set to miss Poland's Nations League group stage matches against Bosnia and Herzegovina, with media reports saying the keeper faces up to seven months on the sidelines.
"I’m not going to lie, this is not something I ever wanted to post, but life comes at you fast sometimes," Grabara wrote on Instagram, posting a picture of himself on a hospital bed.
After joining Juventus on loan from Wolfsburg in August, Grabara debuted for the Serie A side on Thursday, providing an assist and winning the player-of-the-match award in a 5-0 Europa League win over NEC Nijmegen.
On Saturday, however, he felt a strain in his right knee during training, and tests revealed he had suffered an ACL tear.
Local media reported that Juventus were nearing a deal with 37-year-old Brazilian Neto, who played for the club from 2015 to 2017, as Grabara's replacement.

items.title: Victims of alleged abuse by Slovenian priest urge Pope Leo to expedite Church trial
items.summary: VATICAN CITY, Sept 23 - Five victims of alleged abuse by a prominent priest with Vatican ties urged Pope Leo on Wednesday to press for the conclusion of a nearly year-long Church trial of the cleric, saying a lengthy and secret process was denying them justice.
items.body_text:
Victims of alleged abuse by Slovenian priest urge Pope Leo to expedite Church trial
VATICAN CITY, Sept 23 - Five victims of alleged abuse by a prominent priest with Vatican ties urged Pope Leo on Wednesday to press for the conclusion of a nearly year-long Church trial of the cleric, saying a lengthy and secret process was denying them justice.
In an open letter ahead of Leo's four-day visit to France, where the pope is hoping to repair the Church's standing after abuse scandals there, victims of Rev. Marko Rupnik said their treatment reflects poorly on the Church's commitment to helping victims.
"This is the message being conveyed ... that it is useless to report abuse to ecclesiastical authorities, because nothing happens anyway and no one will be held accountable," read the letter.
The victims said they had received no updates about the Church trial and had not been able to offer testimony.
They urged Leo to press for a fair trial "so that the judgment and its outcome, whatever it may be, will remain free of any shadow of doubt."
The Vatican press office did not immediately offer comment.
Rupnik, a Slovenian priest, is a religious artist whose mosaics adorn about 200 churches and chapels around the world, including a basilica in Lourdes, France, where the pope will visit on Saturday.
The bishop of Lourdes has ordered that the mosaics be covered up for the pope's visit.
More than 20 women, mostly former nuns, have accused Rupnik of sexual and psychological abuse.
The priest, expelled from the Jesuit order in 2023 after it found the accusations against him to be "very highly" credible, is not known to have commented publicly on the allegations.
The head of the Vatican's powerful doctrinal office first announced a Church trial against Rupnik in October 2025. Such trials are held behind closed doors and there have been few updates since. In July, the Vatican denied reports that a decision had been made in the case. REUTERS

items.title: Tigrayan leaders say new war with Ethiopian government has begun, as fighting erupts
items.summary: Sept 23 - The leaders of the northern Ethiopian region of Tigray said on Wednesday that they had entered a new war with the federal government as fighting broke out in Tigray and two neighbouring regions, shattering a four-year-old peace deal.
items.body_text:
Tigrayan leaders say new war with Ethiopian government has begun, as fighting erupts
Sept 23 - The leaders of the northern Ethiopian region of Tigray said on Wednesday that they had entered a new war with the federal government as fighting broke out in Tigray and two neighbouring regions, shattering a four-year-old peace deal.
A 2020-2022 civil war between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and federal forces resulted in hundreds of thousands of deaths before the Pretoria Agreement was signed in November 2022.
The outbreak of new fighting follows months of growing animosity between the two sides, capped by Sunday's announcement that the TPLF had formed an alliance with six other armed groups from across Ethiopia aimed at overthrowing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.
"Following the intensification of the invasion conducted through various methods by Abiy Ahmed’s autocratic and genocidal Prosperity regime against the people of Tigray... the Tigray National Regional Government announced that the Tigray Forces have been instructed to counter the attack and have entered a defensive war," the TPLF-led regional administration said in a statement.
Getachew Reda, an adviser to Abiy and a former TPLF official, wrote on X that the TPLF had seized control of federally controlled airports in Tigray and launched an "all out offensive" against government positions in the neighbouring regions of Afar and Amhara.
Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to the region.
ARMED GROUPS SIDE WITH TIGRAYANS
Four sources, including a senior Ethiopian government official, a diplomatic source, a humanitarian source and another source with links to the TPLF and an allied militia, confirmed the developments in Tigray, Afar and Amhara.
They said that in Afar, Tigrayan forces were fighting alongside a local armed group, and that in Amhara, they were fighting alongside the Fano militia.
Fano sided with the federal government during the 2020-2022 war, but rose up against it in 2023. It is a member of the new alliance with the TPLF.
Spokespeople for Abiy, the federal government and the TPLF did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Wednesday. The federal government has accused the TPLF of violating the Pretoria Agreement and seeking to create chaos.
Abiy's spokesperson, Billene Seyoum, told Reuters on Monday that members of the newly announced alliance had been collaborating for a while with the financial backing of Ethiopia's neighbour and historic adversary Eritrea.
Eritrea has repeatedly denied accusations it supports Ethiopian armed groups. Its information minister declined to comment on Wednesday about the latest developments. REUTERS

items.title: US stresses backing for Asian allies
items.body_text:
- 
            US stresses backing for Asian alliesCALL: US, Japanese and South Korean foreign ministers expressed support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in appropriate international organizations
  - Reuters, NEW YORK
 The US on Monday reiterated its commitment to the defense of key Asian allies Japan and South Korea, and the three nations expressed support for Taiwan ahead of a summit this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平). Analysts say the US allies are anxious that Trump might offer concessions to Xi including over Taiwan and trade in return for an economic win with Beijing when he hosts the Chinese president at the White House in Washington tomorrow. Officials say Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and South Korean President Lee Jae-myung are keen to see the US president during the UN General Assembly in New York, where all three were scheduled to speak yesterday. From left, South Korean Minister of Foreign Affairs Cho Hyun, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi pose for a photograph ahead of their talks in New York on Monday.Photo: EPA US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday met with his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun and Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs Toshimitsu Motegi in New York. They issued a joint statement vowing, in apparent reference to China, to stand firm “against economic coercion and non-market policies and practices” and “arbitrary export restrictions that disrupt supply chains.” They also welcomed the launch of a new trilateral consultation mechanism on economic security, part of broader efforts to strengthen supply chains and cooperation on critical technologies. The statement said the US “reiterated its ironclad commitments to the defense of Japan and the ROK [Republic of Korea], backed by America’s unmatched military strength, including its nuclear capabilities, and reaffirmed its extended deterrence commitments to Japan and the ROK,” referring to South Korea’s official name.   - By Lee I-chia / Staff reporter
 The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) yesterday said that 165 severe flu cases and 30 flu-related deaths were reported last week, the highest weekly numbers in this flu season, and that cases might continue to increase, urging people to take precautions. Medical visits for flu-like illnesses increased by 1.4 percent to 141,374 last week, with 11.8 percent being emergency visits, showing that the seasonal flu is still in its epidemic period, CDC Epidemic Intelligence Center Director Guo Hung-wei (郭宏偉) said. From Tuesday last week to Monday, 165 severe flu cases and 30 flu-related deaths were confirmed, the highest weekly numbers since October last year, and also the highest numbers of the same week in five years, he said. Centers for Disease Control Deputy Director-General Lin Ming-cheng, center, holds a news conference in Taipei yesterday.Photo: Hou Chia-yu, Taipei Times Of the accumulated 1,586 severe cases and 304 flu-related deaths in this flu season, 65.8 percent were people aged 65 or older, and 83.2 percent had chronic diseases, he said, adding that elderly people with underlying conditions have the highest risk of developing severe illness. Among the latest confirmed flu deaths, the youngest was a five-year-old boy who did not have underlying health conditions, but also did not get vaccinated, CDC physician Lin Yung-ching (林詠青) said. The boy began having flu-like symptoms late last month and first sought treatment at a clinic, but as he later developed recurring fever, altered consciousness and convulsions, he was referred to a hospital for emergency treatment, Lin said. At the hospital he was confirmed to be infected with influenza A virus and showed signs of encephalitis, he said. The boy remained unconscious for more than two weeks in an intensive care unit and died of influenza-induced acute necrotizing encephalopathy combined with sepsis, he said. Contact tracing found that a person living with the boy had also contracted the flu late last month, Lin said. Guo said medical visits for COVID-19 increased 20.6 percent to 14,462 last week, and 48 severe cases and nine deaths were confirmed from Tuesday last week to Monday. Among the deaths was a man in his 30s, who had multiple chronic health conditions, and he died of cardiogenic shock and septic shock about two weeks after hospitalization, Lin said. As transmittable respiratory diseases typically become more active when temperatures drop, the CDC urge people to practice hand and respiratory hygiene, he said. Infected high-risk people, including young children, people with chronic conditions and older people, should also seek medical attention as soon as possible, especially if they develop symptoms such as difficulty breathing and altered consciousness, he said. Flu cases are expected to rise to a peak of 150,000 to 160,000 weekly medical visits, CDC Deputy Director-General Lin Min-cheng (林明誠) said. There is an increased infection risk as people congregate during the upcoming Mid-Autumn Festival, Lin Min-cheng said. items.title: Chiang, Shen neck-and-neck in Taipei, poll suggests
items.body_text:
- 
            Chiang, Shen neck-and-neck in Taipei, poll suggests
  - By Lin Che-yuan / Staff reporter
 A poll released yesterday suggested that Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安) of the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) and Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) Legislator Puma Shen (沈伯洋) are neck-and-neck in the Taipei mayoral race. The poll asked Taipei residents: “With just more than two months remaining before the Taipei mayoral election, six candidates have reportedly registered to run. If the election were held now, who would you most likely vote for?” The results showed that 41.7 percent said they would vote for Chiang, 40.5 percent for Shen, 0.7 percent for Kuo Hsi (郭璽) of the Taiwan Mahjong Greatest Party, 0.6 percent for Tang Hsin-min (唐新民) of the Three Forces Unity Promotion Alliance, 0.5 percent for Hsiao Wen-chien (蕭文乾) of the MiLinguall Party and 0.3 percent for independent candidate Lin Chih-cheng (林志成). On the other hand, 5.2 percent said they would not vote or would cast an invalid ballot, while 10.6 percent gave no answer. Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an, front, second right, signs an autograph during a visit to a traditional market in Taipei’s Wanhua District yesterday.Photo: CNA Through cross-analysis, the results suggested people aged 50 or above tended to support Chiang, while those aged 20 to 49 tended to support Shen. In terms of political leaning, 96.1 percent of KMT supporters said they intended to vote for Chiang, compared with 88.5 percent of Taiwan People’s Party supporters, the poll showed. Meanwhile 89.4 percent of DPP supporters said they would vote for Shen. Democratic Progressive Party Legislator and Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen, center, high-fives with supporters at Yanshan Night Market in Taipei last night.Photo: Lo Pei-de, Taipei Times Among politically unaffiliated voters, 31.7 percent said they would back Chiang and 25.9 percent said they would vote for Shen, while 12.1 percent said they did not plan to vote and 27.4 percent remained undecided or declined to give an answer, the poll showed. A gender breakdown of the figures suggested male voters favored Shen at 43.3 percent to Chiang’s 41.0 percent, while Chiang held a decisive lead among female voters, capturing 42.3 percent support over Shen’s 38.1 percent, a 4.2 percentage-point margin. The poll was commissioned by the Taipei Trust in Democracy Association, designed and analyzed by polling expert Tai Li-an (戴立安), and conducted by Beacon Market Research from Wednesday to Friday last week. It surveyed 1,076 people aged 20 or older, with 752 interviews conducted via landline and 324 via mobile phone. It has a margin of error of 3.0 percentage points. Chiang yesterday said that “any numbers are merely for reference,” adding that the municipal team’s top priority remains steadily advancing city affairs. Shen expressed confidence in Tai’s long-established credibility. “If anyone wants to question the validity of a poll, they should simply present scientific evidence,” Shen said. “Slapping labels on it arbitrarily is meaningless. It is crucial that we stick to professional standards,” he said, referring to criticism over the association’s alleged ties to United Microelectronics Corp founder Robert Tsao (曹興誠), who had donated to the civil defense organization Kuma Academy founded by Shen and worked closely with Shen during the recall campaign against KMT lawmakers last year. Association founder and chairman Huang Ching-lung (黃清龍) yesterday said he cofounded the organization with like-minded friends, adding that the poll was directly commissioned and funded by the association. Tai said that having conducted polling for organizations across the political spectrum, the key lies in maintaining complete transparency by publicly disclosing the survey’s methodology, design and authorship. Taipei City Councilor Liu Tsai-wei (柳采葳) of the KMT voiced doubts about the survey’s sampling structure, calling the heavily green-leaning skew — 37.5 percent pan-green

items.title: Hong Kong considers heavier fines for pet abandonment following fatal Yuen Long dog attack
items.summary: Hong Kong authorities are considering heavier fines for pet abandonment, the environment minister has said as an operation to capture stray dogs after a fatal dog attack in Yuen Long continued. Secretary for Environment and Ecology Tse Chin-wan said during a Legislative Council meeting on Wednesday that dog owners bear responsibility for their pets, and […]
items.body_text:
Hong Kong authorities are considering heavier fines for pet abandonment, the environment minister has said as an operation to capture stray dogs after a fatal dog attack in Yuen Long continued.
Secretary for Environment and Ecology Tse Chin-wan said during a Legislative Council meeting on Wednesday that dog owners bear responsibility for their pets, and that there should be consequences if they give them up.
“By the end of the year, we will inform this committee whether there is a need to increase penalties for [pet] abandonment,” Tse said in Cantonese.
His comments followed a dog attack in Yuen Long on Saturday that left a 27-year-old woman dead.
See also: ‘Deed, not breed’: Owners and experts push back on stigma against ‘fighting dogs’
The victim was cycling late at night after renting a bike outside an MTR station when three dogs chased her, police said, adding that officers had reviewed CCTV footage.
She was not breathing by the time paramedics arrived, and was certified dead at the hospital.
5 dogs captured
Since the mauling, police and the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) have conducted at least three sweeps around Pok Wai South Road, where the incident took place, to identify dogs that could be aggressive.
So far, authorities have captured five stray dogs, three of which are microchipped.
By law, dog owners must microchip their dogs as part of the dog licensing procedure.
Two of the dogs, both mongrels that did not appear to have owners, were captured on Tuesday night.
The AFCD said on social media that all captured animals would be taken to the department’s centre for observation.
Last month, a number of rare fatal dog attacks made headlines and prompted authorities to review the city’s regulations relating to canines.
In August, a dog – reportedly a Spanish mastiff – killed two smaller dogs in separate incidents in Yuen Long.
A woman working at a dog shelter in Ta Kwu Ling was also killed by a dog that the AFCD later said was a “fighting dog,” a legal term that refers to specific dog types with a history of being bred for dog fighting.
Fighting dogs – encompassing Pit Bull Terriers, Dogo Argentinos, Japanese Tosas, and Fila-Brasileiro – are subject to strict rules, including having to be muzzled in public. They are also barred from dog-friendly restaurants.

items.summary: China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said. The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade. items.body_text:
China’s leader Xi Jinping departed Beijing on Wednesday, bound for Washington where he will meet with US President Donald Trump, state media said.
The highly anticipated talks come as the two countries confront rising fears about increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems, and as both sides look to ease tensions on trade.
Xi “left Beijing by special plane”, accompanied by his wife Peng Liyuan, his right-hand man Cai Qi, and foreign minister Wang Yi, among others, state broadcaster CCTV said.
Trump is due to personally meet Xi on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews, before their meetings on Thursday, according to the White House.
The US leader was greeted by China’s vice president when he landed in Beijing for his state visit in May.
Xi and Peng will attend a ceremony at the White House on Thursday morning, which will include a military flyover.
The two leaders are due to hold talks and Trump is set to host Xi for a state dinner at the White House in the evening.
The visit will wrap up on Friday morning where the two presidential couples will have tea at the White House then visit the National Archives to round out the trip.
The White House said that the visit marks “a significant milestone in the relationship between the two countries.”
But the meeting between the two leaders could touch on multiple points of tension, with Trump telling reporters that he will be “discussing almost everything” with Xi.
Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran — despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.
A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs.
The threat of war over the island of Taiwan — which China claims as its territory — looms large as well.
Leverage
Analysts, however, have tempered expectations by cautioning there might not be many concrete deals announced.
Preliminary talks between US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng discussed creating a communication channel for AI concerns, but released little in the way of detail.
Bessant said at the time that the two sides discussed setting up a way to communicate about AI issues called the “US-China AI dialogue.”
“The US has proposed that we have a notification mechanism between the two countries,” Bessent said.
The son of jailed Hong Kong pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai made an appeal to Xi from Washington that his 78-year-old father be released.
Trump said in May, however, that he had discussed Lai’s fate with Xi and his release was unlikely.
But Beijing did release the founder of an underground church, Ezra Jin, after Trump raised his case with Xi.
China’s negotiating arsenal includes its dominance in the supply of rare earths, critical materials used for high-tech products that are vital to US manufacturers.
Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths.

items.body_text:
Singapore’s entry-level job market shrinks despite salary growth, data shows
Aon data published last month shows a 3.2 per cent drop in entry-level headcount in the city state, amid a rise in AI use in the workplace
Data published last month by global professional services firm Aon showed a 2.5 per cent year-on-year salary increase for entry-level employees, alongside a 3.2 per cent drop in entry-level headcount.
The findings come as graduate employment in Singapore has also weakened. A joint survey by the country’s six autonomous universities released in March found that 83.4 per cent of recent graduates who sought jobs were working within six months of their final exams, declining from 87.1 per cent in 2024 and continuing a downward trend since 2022.
Aon’s findings also point to a shift in employer expectations for new workforce entrants, as artificial intelligence takes on a growing role in the workplace.

items.body_text:
不是台胞證！赴中「4種證件」一申請即刻失去台灣身分
只要台灣人民取得台灣居民定居證、中國居民身分證、中國護照、中國邊境旅遊護照這4種證件，將等同於放棄在台灣的法律身分。（資料照）
赴中旅遊或交流務必注意身分紅線！陸委會示警，依《兩岸人民關係條例》規範，台灣人民不得在中國設立戶籍或領用中國護照，違者將喪失台灣身分，並由戶政機關廢止台灣戶籍、註銷身分證與護照。其中，有「4種證件」一旦申請，恐直接踩雷，慘遭除籍。
觸法「4大紅線證件」盤點：
台灣居民定居證
「台灣居民定居證」（簡稱定居證），為中國推動台人落戶政策所發予的前置文件，主要用於辦理常住戶口登記，取得該證即被認定為「同意在中國設立戶籍」，將喪失在台身分。
中國居民身分證
取得「中國居民身分證」，也就代表已在中國完成常住戶籍登記並取得身分，一經查獲將立即由戶政機關予以廢止台灣戶籍，全面註銷身分證與護照。
中國護照
依《兩岸人民關係條例》規定，台灣人民不得領用「中國護照」。只要查證持有中國正式護照，地方行政機關將直接廢止台灣戶籍與相關公民權利。
中國邊境旅遊護照
「中國邊境旅遊護照」經常被不肖旅行社以「方便通關」、「免排隊代辦簽證」等宣傳手段包裝，讓旅客誤認為只是暫時性通行文件。陸委會強調，即使該護照效期僅3個月且限邊境旅遊，其法律效力仍屬中國公安機關核發「公民」的正式護照，一旦申辦同樣會被廢止在台戶籍。
台胞證不違法 但仍須防範人身安全
民眾最常使用的「台胞證」（台灣居民來往大陸通行證），僅屬旅行證件，並非設籍證明，單純持有並不違反兩岸條例，無須恐慌。
不過陸委會也提醒，即使台胞證合法，中共近年常將持證者視為其公民，加上中國擴大國安審查、收緊出入境與邊境控管規範，赴中即使未違法，也可能遭遇「邊控」或限制離境。民眾前往中國除了勿申請上述4種證件外，也應審慎評估人身安全與潛在風險。

            根據「電腦網路內容分級處理辦法」修正條文第六條第三款規定，已於網站首頁或各該限制級網頁，依台灣網站分級推廣基金會規定作標示。 台灣網站分級推廣基金會（TICRF）網站：http://www.ticrf.org.tw
        
    衛武營10/3當代歌劇《Miedka：野性面容》演繹生死邊緣的狂野蛻變
《Miedka：野性面容》劇照。（衛武營提供）
〔記者陳文嬋／高雄報導〕衛武營國家藝術文化中心將於10月3日推出《Miedka：野性面容》，靈感起源人類學家馬汀遭熊襲傷倖存，亞歷山大．李維以當代歌劇形式，結合人聲、獸鳴等視聽震撼，演繹生死邊緣的狂野蛻變，帶領觀眾彷彿身歷其境，感受大自然深不可測力量。
《Miedka：野性面容》劇照。（衛武營提供）
「Miedka」是俄羅斯堪察加半島原住民埃文人（Évènes）特殊辭彙，意指「半人半獸」狀態，在埃文族人世界觀中，人和熊可以彼此影響、互相轉化。人類學家馬汀劫後餘生，感受到靈魂變異，彷彿成為一半是熊、一半是女人存在，將這段心路歷程完整記錄於著作《相信野獸》，成為全劇靈感來源。
《Miedka：野性面容》劇照。（衛武營提供）
《Miedka：野性面容》打破傳統歌劇疆界，匯聚充滿張力的電子音樂、埃文族與阿伊努族歌唱元素，並採集堪察加半島野生動物錄音，結合視覺藝術家打造裝置藝術，形成各種感官元素在空間中交織疊加，將原本難以言喻的創傷與蛻變，具象化為充滿野性與生命力的視聽震撼，帶領觀眾深入探索人類與大自然之間的狂野力量。
《Miedka：野性面容》劇照。（衛武營提供）
全劇也是一件互動式裝置藝術，由衛武營「混青春表演課」學員合唱團登台獻聲，這群來自不同領域跨世代學員，將於劇中化身為充滿神秘色彩「夢境之聲」，不同年齡世代相遇、交流，共同詮釋跨越物種的生命體驗，與台灣土地產生更深連結。
衛武營也將於10月9至18日推出《Miedka：野性面容》互動裝置展，呈現跨越物種的生命體驗，讓觀眾近距離接觸，感受跨越人類與大自然的生命力。

items.body_text:
社工侵吞長者1200萬 王婉諭轟：北市社會局螺絲鬆掉了
時代力量黨主席王婉諭。（資料照）
台北市社會局38歲社工督導江羿潔涉嫌利用職務之便，侵吞5名無法自行管理財產的受監護長者逾1200萬元，引起社會譁然。對此，時代力量黨主席王婉諭指出，台北市社會局的螺絲真的鬆掉了，該案最該被檢討的，就是整個社會局混亂的制度和顢頇的高層，「蔣萬安市長，你應該好好審視社會局的內控機制，不要讓高層的怠惰，抹煞了基層社工的努力」。
王婉諭在臉書發文表示，台北市社會局的螺絲真的鬆掉了，目前查出的受害者有5位，都是文山區受監護宣告的長者，他們大多因為年紀大、失智，且沒有家人可以聯繫，所以由國家來代管財產。這位督導去年5月到職，負責保存這些長輩的帳戶、存摺、印章及現金，結果他卻利用這個機會趁虛而入，侵佔每人平均約240萬，而且完全沒被發現，直到今年6月，她主動離職後，社會局在清點個案財產的過程，才發現帳目短缺。
王婉諭指出，有幾個疑點，社會局現在應該說清楚，第一是「為什麼同一個人，可以同時保管、提領、核銷財產？」她的職務內容是保管存摺、保管印章、代為處理財產事務，也就是說：保管、經手、支用的人，有可能都是同一個，這在任何會碰到錢的單位，都是難以想像的事情，社會局應該解釋清楚。
王婉諭再指，第二是「這一年之內，沒有任何查核機制嗎？」社會局直到交接時才發現異常，換句話說，如果她不離職，根本不會被發現，負責代管他人數百萬元財產的業務，台北市社會局這一整年沒有任何一次抽查嗎？
王婉諭質疑，第三是「台北市現在到底代管了多少位長者？」社會局擔任監護人的個案有幾位？代管的財產總額多少？存摺和印章現在由誰保管？多久查一次？最近一次全面盤點是什麼時候？
她認為，北市社會局「老人福利科」早就問題百出，2025年2月，有社工透過衛福部的勞動申訴平台，檢舉台北市某長照基金會未給付1.5個月年終，台北市社會局查了兩個月之後，要求單位補發，但在2025年底的列管會議上，台北市社會局卻完全無法回應工會的問題，因此主席要求重新查察。
王婉諭說，結果這一查就查了8個月，一直上月台北市府才完成調查結果，結果顯示北市社會局老福科根本沒有落實稽查、沒有追究不實核銷，也沒有依規定停止補助，調查中還提到，就是因為「老人福利科」人事頻繁更換，所以才導致調查中斷。
王婉諭怒轟，這位社工督導已經認罪，根本就是社工界的老鼠屎，因為絕大多數的社工，每天處理的是別人生命中最難的時刻，領著不高的薪水，背著超量的案子，還要面對積欠的費用、混亂的行政，和隨時可能被檢討的壓力，他們沒有穿金戴銀，他們都身心俱疲。
她指出，所以最該被檢討的，就是整個社會局混亂的制度和顢頇的高層，近期台北市已經發生一連串的社福漏洞，「蔣萬安市長，你應該好好審視社會局的內控機制，不要讓高層的怠惰，抹煞了基層社工的努力」。

items.title: Collapse at factory-run coal mine in North Hamgyong province injures worker
items.summary: A coal mine collapse in North Korea’s North Hamgyong province on Sept. 12 seriously injured one worker. The accident highlights how production pressure is outpacing safety measures as winter approaches. A source in North Hamgyong province told Daily NK recently that the accident occurred at a mine run by a machinery factory. Timber supports holding […]
items.body_text:
A coal mine collapse in North Korea’s North Hamgyong province on Sept. 12 seriously injured one worker. The accident highlights how production pressure is outpacing safety measures as winter approaches.
A source in North Hamgyong province told Daily NK recently that the accident occurred at a mine run by a machinery factory. Timber supports holding up an inclined shaft gave way as workers were heading in for their shift. An inclined shaft is a sloping tunnel that leads from the surface to the underground coal face.
“Three workers on their way in were buried under the dirt,” the source said. “One of them was taken to a hospital with serious injuries to his lower back and legs.”
Workers reportedly walk down the shaft for 40 minutes to an hour to reach the underground work area. “Many of the supports are weak, so nobody knows when the ceiling will come down,” the source said. “Just going to and from the work site is extremely dangerous in itself.”
Coal mine collapse highlights worker safety gaps as winter nears
The factory, which produces machinery for coal mines, operates the mine to secure its own coal supply. The factory mainly uses the coal for heating and cooking at its sanatorium and workers’ dormitories. A factory sanatorium is a company-run rest and recuperation facility for employees.
The mine normally runs on day shifts, but night work is added when the factory party committee pushes for more coal. Workers then reportedly work night shifts lasting two to three days at a time. Factory party committees are local branches of the Workers’ Party of Korea (WPK) that oversee management and production drives. According to the source, these demands grow louder ahead of winter, when the factory must stockpile coal for its facilities.
Even so, the mine shows little sign of replacing old timber supports or reinforcing risky sections of the shaft. With the mine even responsible for procuring its own work tools, safety inevitably falls down the list of priorities.
“Higher-ups keep pressing us to dig more coal before winter,” the source said. “But they show no interest in replacing or reinforcing the old supports. Workers have to carry out their production tasks while worrying that the shaft could collapse at any time.”
Work at the mine has temporarily stopped since the accident. The source expects the factory to follow a familiar pattern this time. “Because they are desperate to meet coal quotas, they often fix only the spot that collapsed and put people back to digging instead of dealing with every dangerous section,” he said.
“With work continuing into the night, workers pile up fatigue and struggle to spot dangers in time,” he added. “The mine is so outdated that an accident would not be surprising at any time.” The source said concern over further accidents is also growing.
Reporting from inside North Korea
Daily NK operates networks of sources inside North Korea who document events in real-time and transmit information through secure channels. Unlike reporting based on state media, satellite imagery, or defector accounts from years past, our journalism comes directly from people currently living under the regime. We verify reports through multiple independent sources and cross-reference details before publication.
Our sources remain anonymous because contact with foreign media is treated as a capital offense in North Korea — discovery means imprisonment or execution. This network-based approach allows Daily NK to report on developments other outlets cannot access: market trends, policy implementation, public sentiment, and daily realities that never appear in official narratives.
Maintaining these secure communication channels and protecting source identities requires specialized protocols and constant vigilance. Daily NK serves as a bridge between North Koreans and the outside world, documenting what’s happening inside one of the world’s most closed societies.

items.title: Diverted military morphine raises health fears for North Korean officer’s wife
items.summary: A North Korean army officer has spent years diverting morphine meant for military medical facilities to his wife. A source inside the military told Daily NK recently that her health has since raised concern among other officers’ families. The officer works at a rear supply depot under the Fourth Corps, a large army command based […]
items.body_text:
A North Korean army officer has spent years diverting morphine meant for military medical facilities to his wife. A source inside the military told Daily NK recently that her health has since raised concern among other officers’ families.
The officer works at a rear supply depot under the Fourth Corps, a large army command based in South Hwanghae province. Rear supply depots store and distribute medicine, food and other necessities to army units. This depot holds drugs bound for unit clinics and other military medical facilities. They include morphine, a powerful opioid used as a painkiller and an anesthetic.
“His wife has been using the morphine he gave her for three to four years,” the source said. “Recently she has become noticeably thin and even the shape of her legs has changed.”
According to the source, the officer has habitually taken morphine from the depot by using his rank and position. His wife often suffers from headaches and took the drug without a doctor’s diagnosis or prescription. She gradually increased her use, saying, “When I use morphine, the pain goes away and my body feels comfortable.”
Morphine is a strong opioid painkiller, and repeated or excessive use can cause tolerance and dependence. Users may need larger doses for the same pain relief, and stopping can bring anxiety and insomnia.
Families of other officers have urged her to visit a hospital for tests, but she reportedly brushes off their concerns. She has not had a thorough medical examination, so it is unclear whether her changes stem from morphine use. Long-term use can generally cause side effects such as loss of appetite and weight loss. Bowed legs, however, could also result from malnutrition, fractures or joint and nervous system disorders.
“She keeps getting thinner and even her way of walking has changed,” the source said. “Yet she is the only one who says she is fine.” Some around her even wonder whether the morphine is keeping her from properly sensing that something is wrong with her body, the source added.
Weak controls on morphine in North Korea’s military
Diverting morphine for private use over several years without anyone raising concerns has drawn criticism. Critics say oversight of military medical supplies and discipline among officials is seriously flawed. Unit clinics frequently fail to receive medicine on time, and narcotic drugs such as morphine require strict usage records. Even so, the diversion went unchecked for years, critics say.
The source said the officer’s management role makes it difficult for anyone below to challenge him. The case appears to show how corruption and weak drug controls in the North Korean military can create public health risks.
“An official’s family has used medicine meant for ordinary soldier patients,” the source said. “If that becomes known, the depot’s entire medicine management could come under scrutiny.”

Rice prices in North Korea’s informal markets, known as jangmadang, continued falling in September 2026 after a stretch of national holidays boosted grain supplies and eased demand.
According to Daily NK’s regular survey of North Korean market prices, a kilogram of rice sold for 41,100 North Korean won in one Pyongyang market as of Sept. 13. That was down 8.9% from the previous survey on Aug. 30.
Prices fell by similar margins in Sinuiju, North Pyongan province, and Hyesan, Ryanggang province. Rice sold for 41,200 won per kilogram in Sinuiju and 41,400 won in Hyesan. The prices were down 8.8% and 8.6%, respectively, from two weeks earlier.
Corn, a staple food for lower-income North Korean people, also dropped noticeably in price. In Hyesan, a kilogram of corn cost 16,700 won, down 7.2% over the same two-week period.
The 4% to 9% decline in grain prices appears tied to increased supply around the Sept. 9 regime founding anniversary and the Chuseok harvest holiday. That extra supply reduced demand at markets during the period.
Ahead of major holidays, North Korean institutions typically supply cadres and employees with rice, corn, flour, cooking oil and sugar. That practice appears to have both curbed market demand and pushed extra grain into markets, contributing to the price drop.
The arrival of this year’s freshly harvested corn also appears to be weighing on grain prices.
“This is the season when freshly harvested corn for eating reaches the market,” Cho Chung-hee, director of the Good Farmers research institute, told Daily NK by phone. “While the new corn supply continues, corn prices, and rice prices to some extent, tend to fall somewhat,” she said. “This recent decline in prices appears to reflect that same trend.”
Dollar holds steady as yuan rate posts sharpest drop of the year
Foreign exchange rates showed diverging trends for the dollar and the Chinese yuan this month. The dollar exchange rate held firm with a slight upward bias, while the yuan exchange rate fell sharply.
The dollar exchange rate in Pyongyang’s markets stood at 69,500 won as of Sept. 13, up 1.9% from two weeks earlier, with Sinuiju and Hyesan showing similar trends.
By contrast, the won-yuan exchange rate fell around 12.5% over the same period in all three cities surveyed. The rate reached 12,500 won in Pyongyang, 12,530 won in Sinuiju and 12,540 won in Hyesan.
The won-yuan exchange rate started the year in the low 5,000s. It had climbed steadily since then amid warming North Korea-China relations and expanding cross-border trade. This month’s sharp pullback marks the first such decline so far in 2026.
A source said some inside the country increasingly argue the yuan is overvalued. The source described the drop as a correction aimed at rebalancing the relative value of the dollar and the yuan.
The dollar-yuan cross rate inside North Korea has typically hovered between 5.8 and 6.3 yuan per dollar. But as trade with China expanded recently, demand for yuan surged. That pushed the cross rate down to as low as 4.7 yuan per dollar at one point, underscoring the currency’s newfound strength inside the country.
That stands in sharp contrast to the international dollar-yuan exchange rate, which has hovered around 6.8 yuan per dollar. The gap suggests the yuan has been considerably overvalued inside North Korea’s foreign currency market.
The dollar-yuan cross rate inside the country tends to converge within a certain range. That happens because both foreign currencies circulate together in markets and influence each other’s relative value.
When the yuan’s value rises too sharply, it raises the cost of securing yuan needed to pay for Chinese goods. That can deepen imbalances across the broader foreign currency market.
Analysts say the correction reflects market pressure to deflate an excessive yuan valuation and restore a more balanced ratio with the dollar.

items.title: Fans throng to Dockers HQ for last home training before grand final
items.summary: There was so much demand from fans to watch the Dockers train before the grand final, the team made it a ticketed event.
items.body_text:
Thu, 3 Sept, 8:10 pm, Final score, Dockers 40, Hawks 72
Thousands cheer Dockers at their last WA drill before AFL grand final
Thousands of Fremantle Dockers fans have packed out the club's headquarters to watch the team train for the last time in Western Australia before they head to Melbourne for Saturday's AFL grand final.
It has been 13 years since the Dockers last made a grand final, and the open training session in Cockburn saw so much demand that the team ticketed the event.
All 3,000 tickets were sold.
Long-term supporter Katie said the Dockers' success this year had special significance for her and her son Finlay.
Finlay was just six weeks old when the 2013 grand final was held. Two years later, he developed cancer, and relapsed a year later.
"It's 10 years now since his relapse," Katie said.
"So it's his year and it's the Dockers' year, and all he wants is the Dockers to win on grand final day … that's his celebration."
Imogen Somerville, who has also supported the Dockers "her entire life", described the event as overwhelming.
"It was really cool to be able to get down here," she said.
"It was like five bucks to get in, which was awesome, so couldn't miss out on that."
Doing the right thing
Fans cheered the team on the field, then posed for photographs with their football heroes, who signed jerseys, posters and autographs.
And it was not just the public who were in the stands — past players, the club's chief executive Simon Garlick and Deputy Premier Rita Saffioti also attended the session.
Lee Spurr, who played in the 2013 grand final, said he felt "nothing but proud" to see his club back in the running for the flag.
"I was pretty nervous watching the prelim, but now that they're there, I feel like I'm almost playing. My phone's been blowing up," he said.
After experiencing the lead-up to the AFL's biggest week, Spurr said it was important for the players to turn off their phones and stick to preparation.
"My advice would be don't get caught up in doing too much, " he said.
"This week's about doing the process, doing what's right and preparing."
Pure excitement
Superstar ruckman Luke Jackson said he loved having the fans participate in the club's biggest week.
"Just pure excitement. Can't wait to get over there and can't wait to play on Saturday in front of all these fans. It will be good fun," he said.
Jackson was in his second AFL season when he won his first premiership with the Melbourne Demons in 2021 in Perth.
He said he was looking forward to playing at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, where the Dockers will face the Brisbane Lions.
Defender Jordan Clark was also excited, and grateful, to see the fans.
"They support us through thick and thin, as they have done for the last 30 years," he said.
"So they're pretty happy with this moment and they rightly deserve to be, so it's pretty special when we get this support."
With no chance of making the training session, dozens of Dockers fans 1,600 kilometres away flocked to Broome airport today to catch the only direct flight to Melbourne before Saturday.
David Leslie, who goes by Docker Dave, has followed the team since its inception said his faith had been “restored” after their stellar final performances against Swans and Geelong.

items.title: Heeney 'extremely thankful' after addressing entire Swans club on return
items.summary: Isaac Heeney speaks publicly for the first time since he was banned by Sydney for breaching the club's standards after the Swans season came to an end.
items.body_text:
Sydney Swans forward Isaac Heeney says he is "thankful" for the opportunity to address his teammates and the club for the first time since he and four other players were suspended.
Heeney and his fellow banned teammates arrived at Swans HQ in Moore Park for their exit meetings on Wednesday evening after Sydney's 2026 season came to an end last week.
"It was really nice to address the whole club," Heeney said in a short statement.
"Extremely thankful they could give us their time and understanding … so yeah, it was really good."
It is Heeney's first public comment since he and four teammates — Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice — were suspended by the club for a breach of standards last month.
Warner and Bice arrived at Swans HQ first before Heeney, Jordon and Blakey arrived as a group shortly afterwards.
Warner was questioned by reporters on whether he would apologise to his teammates and said: "I don't know, we'll wait and see."
The banned players were met at the door by Swans executive general manager of football, Leon Cameron. Blakey, Jordon and Bice did not speak.
No decision has been made by Sydney on the playing futures of the five suspended players beyond this season.
Warner and Jordon are contracted through 2027 while Heeney and Bice are contracted through 2028. Blakey's contract with Sydney runs through the 2031 season.
An undermanned Swans side shocked grand finalists Brisbane in a qualifying final earlier this month before being beaten by Fremantle in last week's preliminary final.

items.summary: Brian To'o and Greg Marzhew have never met a rugby league problem they couldn't solve by running over it and now the two wrecking balls will go head-to-head with an NRL grand final berth on the line.

Brian To'o and Greg Marzhew's NRL finals clash is an unstoppable force against an immovable object
If we're ever going to solve that old question about unstoppable forces and immovable objects, the best way might be letting Brian To'o and Greg Marzhew run straight into each other.
The Penrith and Newcastle wingers will go head-to-head in Sunday's preliminary final with collisions that promise to rock the foundations of Stadium Australia.
Between them they boast a little over 200kg of prime Samoan beef, forged by pumping ludicrous amounts of steel in one case and fuelled by a truly startling quantity of Coke Zero in the other.
With a grand final berth on the line they will do what they do best: taking the ball and smashing into each other and anything else that gets in their way.
They'll do it returning kicks, they'll do it early in sets, they'll do it close to the line to try and barge in and score and they'll do it over and over again until one of them is grand final bound.
Nobody can do all those things, grand finals included, like To'o, which is why he's the best winger of his time, but having played against Marzhew since the two's junior days he'll readily admit to taking some inspiration from the Knights wrecking machine.
"He's someone I like to base my game on, he's really strong and a big part of their team. I'm honoured to battle it out with my uso Greg," said To'o.
"It's our job to put our body on the front line and get the set started. It doesn't matter if it's one person in front of you, or two or three or four or five, just go as hard as you can."
Likewise, Marzhew has looked to To'o plenty of times before and this season has the Panthers legend covered for tries (24 to 16), line breaks (27 to 21) and tackle busts (124 to 112), although To'o has him beat for average run metres (194 per game to 188)
Marzhew's form has earned him Newcastle's player's player award and he believes the challenge of taking on players like To'o has brought out the best in him.
"Penrith are one of my favourite teams to play against, they have so many representative players and I'm getting to go up against one of the best wingers to ever do it," said Marzhew
"I pride myself on that kind of stuff [big carries]. I try to excel with it because it's what the boys expect of me, if the crowd gets on top that's the cherry on top."
He's been doing it for so long now it's hard to imagine a time when To'o didn't relish the contact but he did have to learn to love it.
"When I was a bit younger, I was a bit shorter than I am now, I wouldn't say I was scared but there was that feeling that I might get knocked around," said To'o.
"I don't know if that counts as scared, I guess it pretty much does.
"It wasn't until my old man said, 'You're running it straight and getting knocked down or you're coming off and going home.'
"So I decided I'd run it straight. That was probably under-13s, I just dialled in and decided."
For Marzhew, who's got about 10kg on To'o, the issue was much simpler — there's never been any fear because he has always felt made for this
"Nah, that's the job description [running into people]," said Marzhew.
"That's what I signed up for."
The duo have plenty in common aside from their belief that the best way to solve a rugby league problem is to run right through it.
Both can really put on the dancing shoes — To'o's been hitting a little samba-type number after scoring recently, most notable after wrapping up Penrith's qualifying final over the Roosters with a late intercept try following one of his best games of the season.

"My son does the dance and a Spider-man celebration as well, so I just wanted to honour all the kids.
